docs.title: 🎯 Which layer should you use?
docs.text:
• Most trading apps → MT4Sugar. Risk sizing and auto-normalization protect you from off-quote and invalid-volume rejections.
  • Custom execution → MT4Service. Typed calls when you manage your own sizing/normalization.
  • Protocol-level control → MT4Account. Raw proto structures and streams.

docs.title: Protobuf Inspector
docs.text:
An interactive developer tool that explores the MT4 gRPC protobuf types, fields and enums by reflection — no connection or docs needed to answer "what fields does this type have?" or "what are the valid enum values?".

Source: examples/Tools/ProtobufInspector.cs (class ProtobufInspector). It reflects over the generated mt4_term_api assembly, so it always matches the exact SDK version you have.

docs.title: 🚀 How to run
docs.text:
# reflection-only, no terminal connection (fastest)
dotnet run -- --inspect

# from the examples menu (connects first) → option 12
dotnet run
# or: dotnet run -- --example=inspect

You'll get a > prompt. Type a command (below), or exit to quit.

docs.title: ⌨️ Commands
docs.text: Command What it does list / ls List all *Data / *Request / *Reply types <TypeName> Inspect a type — all properties and their types (collections marked 📚) search <text> / find <text> Find types whose name contains text field <name> Find all types that contain a field (and its type) enum <name> Show an enum's members and numeric values help / ? Full command reference exit / quit / q Leave the inspector

docs.title: 💡 Examples
docs.text:
What fields does AccountSummaryData have? 

> AccountSummaryData
  • AccountBalance      : double
  • AccountEquity       : double
  • AccountMarginFree   : double
  • AccountTradeMode    : EnumAccountTradeMode
  ...

Which types have a Ticket field? 

> field Ticket
📦 OpenedOrderInfo:
   └─ Ticket: int
📦 HistoryOrderInfo:
   └─ Ticket: int
...

What are the order operation values? 

> enum OrderSendOperationType
  OcOpBuy        = 0
  OcOpSell       = 1
  OcOpBuylimit   = 2
  OcOpSelllimit  = 3
  OcOpBuystop    = 4
  OcOpSellstop   = 5

Find everything related to "Order": 

> search Order
  [Class]  OpenedOrderInfo
  [Class]  OrderSendRequest
  [Class]  OrderSendData
  ...

docs.title: 🎯 When it helps
docs.text:
• "Field not found" / wrong name → field <name> shows the correct property and which type has it.
  • Building a Request → inspect the *Request type to see exactly which fields to set.
  • Reading a Reply → inspect the *Data type to see what you can read back.
  • Enum values → enum <Name> instead of guessing (see also the ENUMs Reference).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes
docs.text:
• Reflection-based — it reports the types in your actual MetaRPC.MT4 assembly, so it can't drift from the code.
  • Type names are the C# generated names (e.g. OpenedOrderInfo, QuoteData), matching what you use in code and in the method docs.
  • It's a read-only explorer — it never calls the gateway or places anything.

docs.title: Return Codes & Error Handling
docs.text: How CSharpMT4 reports success and failure. MT4 does not use MT5's numeric returned_code / 10009. Instead, calls either return data (success) or throw ApiExceptionMT4 (failure), carrying classic MT4/MQL error codes.

docs.title: ✅ How success is signalled
docs.text:
• Data methods (AccountSummaryAsync, QuoteAsync, OpenedOrdersAsync, …) — return their typed *Data object. No exception = success.
  • OrderSendAsync — success is a positive Ticket:

var r = await service.OrderSendAsync(req);
if (r.Ticket > 0) Console.WriteLine($"opened #{r.Ticket} @ {r.Price}");
* OrderModifyAsync — OrderModifyData.OrderWasModified == true. * OrderCloseDeleteAsync — succeeds (no throw); Mode says whether a market order was closed or a pending one deleted (OrderCloseDeleteMode).

There is no "check a numeric retcode" step like in MT5. If the gateway/broker rejects the operation, the call throws — wrap trading in try/catch.

docs.title: ⚠️ Failures — ApiExceptionMT4
docs.text:
Any gateway/terminal/broker error is raised as ApiExceptionMT4. It exposes:

Property Type Meaning Error Error The raw proto error object. ErrorType ErrorType Where it came from (see below). ErrorCode string? Gateway error code (string). ErrorMessageText string? Human-readable message. MqlErrorCode MqlErrorCode Classic MT4/MQL error (enum, see below). MqlErrorIntCode int Same error as a raw number. MqlErrorDescription string? MT4 error description. 
try
{
    var r = await service.OrderSendAsync(req);
    Console.WriteLine($"opened #{r.Ticket}");
}
catch (ApiExceptionMT4 ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"rejected: {ex.MqlErrorCode} ({ex.MqlErrorIntCode}) — {ex.MqlErrorDescription ?? ex.ErrorMessageText}");
}

docs.title: ErrorType — error category
docs.text:
• Undefined = 0
  • Mrpc = 1 · MrpcValidation = 2 · MrpcTimeout = 3 — gateway-side (request shape, validation, timeout)
  • TerminalApiTimeout = 4 · TerminalApiGetParams = 5 · TerminalApiSetResult = 6 · TerminalApiUnexpected = 7 — terminal bridge
  • MqlExecution = 8 · MqlCustomExecution = 9 — the MQL/trade server rejected it (read MqlErrorCode)

docs.title: 📋 Common MT4 trade errors (MqlErrorCode)
docs.text:
These are the classic MT4 server/trade codes you'll actually hit. The full enum has 100+ members; the trade-relevant ones:

Code Member Meaning / typical cause 0 ErrNoError success 2 ErrCommonError generic error 3 ErrInvalidTradeParameters bad request fields 4 ErrServerBusy server busy — retry later 6 ErrNoConnection no connection to trade server 8 ErrTooFrequentRequests throttled — slow down 64 ErrAccountDisabled account disabled 65 ErrInvalidAccount invalid account 128 ErrTradeTimeout trade request timed out 129 ErrInvalidPrice price not valid / stale 130 ErrInvalidStops SL/TP too close or wrong side 131 ErrInvalidTradeVolume volume not a valid lot step 132 ErrMarketClosed market closed 133 ErrTradeDisabled trading disabled for symbol/account 134 ErrNotEnoughMoney insufficient free margin 135 ErrPriceChanged price moved — re-send 136 ErrOffQuotes no quotes available 137 ErrBrokerBusy broker busy 138 ErrRequote requote — price changed between quote and send 139 ErrOrderLocked order is locked/being processed 141 ErrTooManyRequests too many requests 145 ErrTradeModifyDenied modification denied (e.g. too close to market) 146 ErrTradeContextBusy trade context busy — retry 147 ErrTradeExpirationDenied pending expiration not allowed 148 ErrTradeTooManyOrders order limit reached

Most of these are broker/market conditions, not SDK bugs. Validate inputs up front: round price to GetDigitsAsync, snap volume to GetVolumeStepAsync, respect GetVolumeMinAsync, and keep SL/TP beyond the broker's minimum stop distance.

docs.title: 🔁 Transient errors the SDK handles for you
docs.text:
You generally don't catch these — MT4Account retries them automatically:

  • gRPC transients: Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal — retried with exponential backoff.
  • Reconnectable terminal errors: e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, TERMINAL_REGISTRY_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND, dead-terminal / readiness-probe conditions — the client reconnects and retries.
  • Stream Cancelled: when you cancel a subscription's token, the Cancelled status is treated as a clean end, not an error.

See gRPC Streaming for stream lifecycle details.

docs.title: 🧩 Handling pattern
docs.text:
try
{
    var r = await service.BuyMarketByRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50);
    Console.WriteLine($"opened #{r.Ticket}");
}
catch (ApiExceptionMT4 ex) when (ex.MqlErrorCode == MqlErrorCode.ErrRequote
                              || ex.MqlErrorCode == MqlErrorCode.ErrPriceChanged)
{
    // price moved — re-read the quote and try again
}
catch (ApiExceptionMT4 ex)
{
    logger.LogWarning("trade rejected: {Code} — {Msg}", ex.MqlErrorCode, ex.MqlErrorDescription);
}
  • Fail fast on logic errors (invalid volume/stops) — fix the request, don't retry.
  • Retry briefly on transient trade errors (ErrRequote, ErrPriceChanged, ErrTradeContextBusy, ErrServerBusy) with a fresh quote.
  • Surface account/market errors (ErrNotEnoughMoney, ErrMarketClosed, ErrTradeDisabled) to the user — retrying won't help.

docs.title: ⚡ Sync vs Async Methods (C#)
docs.text: The CSharpMT4 SDK gives you both synchronous and asynchronous calls — but not on every layer. Which you get depends on where you call from, and the two are not interchangeable everywhere. This guide shows what exists where, and when to use which.

docs.title: 🗺️ What exists where
docs.text:
Layer Async Sync Notes MT4Account (low-level) ✅ …Async ✅ (core calls) Sync twins for the main request/reply calls: AccountSummary, Quote, QuoteMany, Symbols, SymbolParamsMany, TickValueWithSize, QuoteHistory, OpenedOrders, OpenedOrdersTickets, OrdersHistory, OrderSend, OrderModify, OrderCloseDelete, OrderCloseBy, ConnectByServerName, ConnectByHostPort, Disconnect. MT4Service (typed facade) ✅ only ❌ Async-only. MT4Sugar (helpers) ✅ only ❌ Async-only. Streaming (any layer) ✅ only ❌ IAsyncEnumerable<T> — there is no synchronous form.

⚠️ Not every async method has a sync twin. Even on MT4Account, calls like TradeStatsAsync, EquityHistoryAsync, TradeUnrealizedPLAsync and all streams are async-only. The sync list above is the complete set.

docs.title: 🔍 How the sync methods actually work
docs.text:
Each synchronous method is a thin blocking wrapper over its async twin:

// Inside the SDK — the sync method just blocks on the async one:
public AccountSummaryData AccountSummary(DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)
    => AccountSummaryAsync(deadline, ct).GetAwaiter().GetResult();

So the result is identical — the only difference is that the sync version parks the calling thread until the network round trip finishes, while the async version frees it. That single fact drives every recommendation below.

docs.title: ✅ Async — the default for anything real
docs.text:
var account = new MT4Account(user, password, grpcServer, apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync(serverName, "EURUSD");   // 3rd arg is a bool, not a timeout
var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance}, Equity: {summary.AccountEquity}");

Use async for:

  • Bots, services, GUIs — anything that must stay responsive or handle concurrency.
  • Streaming — ticks/trades/P-L are async-only anyway (await foreach).
  • Multi-symbol / parallel work — fire several calls at once (see below).
  • Everything through MT4Service / MT4Sugar — they offer nothing else.

docs.title: 🟡 Sync — fine for simple, linear, one-thread code
docs.text:
var account = new MT4Account(user, password, grpcServer, apiKey);
account.ConnectByServerName(serverName, "EURUSD");
var summary = account.AccountSummary();     // blocks until the reply arrives
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance}");

Reasonable when:

  • A short CLI one-off or setup script that does one thing after another.
  • A REPL / notebook / learning snippet where async plumbing is just noise.
  • You're on MT4Account and don't touch streams.

The sync calls are a convenience, not a performance choice — they are the async calls with a block on top.

docs.title: 🚫 The one rule when mixing
docs.text:
Don't call the sync (blocking) wrappers from inside async code or a UI/sync-context thread. Blocking on a Task that still needs the current context to complete is the classic deadlock, and even when it doesn't deadlock it wastes a thread for the whole round trip.

// ❌ WRONG — inside an async method, don't block with the sync wrapper (or .Result/.Wait())
async Task HandleAsync()
{
    var s = account.AccountSummary();            // blocks this async flow
}

// ✅ RIGHT — in async code, await the async twin
async Task HandleAsync()
{
    var s = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
}

Rule of thumb: in async code, stay async; reach for the sync wrappers only in genuinely synchronous, top-level code.

docs.title: 🔀 Concurrency (async only)
docs.text:
Async lets you run independent calls in parallel instead of back-to-back — something the sync wrappers can't do on one thread:

// All three quotes in flight together, then awaited as one:
var quotes = await Task.WhenAll(
    svc.QuoteAsync("EURUSD"),
    svc.QuoteAsync("GBPUSD"),
    svc.QuoteAsync("USDJPY"));

⚠️ Fan-out is for independent reads. Don't fire overlapping trading operations on the same position concurrently — order them with await.

docs.title: 📡 Streams are async-only
docs.text:
Live subscriptions are IAsyncEnumerable<T>: consume with await foreach, stop with a CancellationToken. There is no synchronous equivalent.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
try
{
    await foreach (var d in svc.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
        Console.WriteLine(d.SymbolTick.Bid);
}
catch (OperationCanceledException) { /* expected on stop */ }

→ Full lifecycle, reconnect and cancellation: gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: 🧯 Common pitfalls
docs.text: Pitfall Why it hurts Fix Sync wrapper (or .Result/.Wait()) inside async code Deadlocks, blocked threads Call the …Async twin and await it Expecting a sync version on MT4Service/MT4Sugar They're async-only — it won't compile Use the async method with await Looking for a sync stream Streams are IAsyncEnumerable only await foreach + CancellationToken async void methods Exceptions can't be awaited/caught Use async Task (except real event handlers) Not awaiting a Task Result used before it's ready; exceptions swallowed Always await

docs.title: 💡 Summary
docs.text:
• MT4Account has sync and async for its core calls; MT4Service / MT4Sugar / streaming are async-only.
  • A sync method is literally …Async().GetAwaiter().GetResult() — same result, but it blocks the thread.
  • Prefer async for bots, services, GUIs, streams and parallelism; use sync only for simple linear scripts on MT4Account.
  • Never block with a sync wrapper (or .Result/.Wait()) inside async code — stay async there.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Getting Started — install, configure, run.
  • gRPC Streaming — the async-only streaming model.
  • Return Codes — handling errors from a call, sync or async.

docs.title: User Code Sandbox
docs.text: A ready-to-edit playground for your own MT4 trading logic — the connection and MT4Service are already wired up, you just fill in the body.

docs.title: 🎯 What it is
docs.text:
The sandbox is the file examples/UserCode/11_ProgramUserCode.cs (class ProgramUserCode). It hands you a connected MT4Service and a base symbol so you can experiment without writing any setup/connection code.

It is wired into the examples menu as 11. USER CODE sandbox.

docs.title: 🚀 How to run
docs.text:
# non-interactive (runs only the sandbox)
dotnet run -- --example=11
# or: dotnet run -- --example=sandbox

# interactive menu → choose 11
dotnet run

Connection settings come from appsettings.json / environment — see Getting Started → Configuration.

docs.title: ✍️ Where to write your code
docs.text:
Open examples/UserCode/11_ProgramUserCode.cs and edit the body of RunAsync between the markers:

public static async Task RunAsync(MT4Service svc, string symbol = "EURUSD", CancellationToken ct = default)
{
    // ── YOUR CODE STARTS HERE ↓ ───────────────────────────────

    // read-only starters (safe):
    var account = await svc.GetAccountSnapshotAsync(ct: ct);
    Console.WriteLine($"Account: {account}");

    var sym = await svc.GetSymbolSnapshotAsync(symbol, ct: ct);
    Console.WriteLine($"Symbol:  {sym}");

    // ── YOUR CODE ENDS HERE ↑ ─────────────────────────────────
}

Everything on svc is available — the typed MT4Service methods and the MT4Sugar extension helpers.

docs.title: 🧪 Examples to drop in
docs.text:
// Sizing math (no orders)
var volume  = await svc.CalcVolumeForRiskAsync(symbol, stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50, ct: ct);
var slPrice = await svc.PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync(symbol, fromAsk: true, offsetPoints: -200, ct: ct);
Console.WriteLine($"risk-sized volume: {volume}, SL: {slPrice}");

// Live tick sample (3 seconds)
using var cts = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct);
cts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3));
try { await foreach (var t in svc.ReadTicks(symbol, cts.Token)) Console.WriteLine($"{t.SymbolTick?.Bid}/{t.SymbolTick?.Ask}"); }
catch (OperationCanceledException) { }

// Trading — UNCOMMENT DELIBERATELY (places real orders)
// var buy = await svc.BuyMarketByRiskAsync(symbol, stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50, ct: ct);
// await svc.ModifySlTpAsync(buy.Ticket, tp: sym.Ask + 400 * sym.Point, ct: ct);
// await svc.CloseByTicketAsync(buy.Ticket, ct: ct);

docs.title: 🔌 Running it standalone (own connection)
docs.text:
Inside the menu the sandbox reuses the already-connected service. To run it outside the menu with its own connection, call the standalone entry point — it connects via ConnectionHelper, runs your RunAsync, then disconnects:

await ProgramUserCode.RunStandaloneAsync("EURUSD");

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Trading is real. Anything that sends/modifies/closes orders acts on the configured account — keep those lines commented until you mean them.
  • Streams need a token. Always bound ReadTicks / ReadTrades with a CancellationToken or timeout.
  • Start read-only. Snapshots, counts and history are safe to run repeatedly while you learn the API.
  • Layer of choice. Use Sugar for one-liners; drop to MT4Service for typed data; drop to MT4Account only when you need the raw request/reply.

docs.title: Your First Project in 10 Minutes (C#)
docs.text: Hands-on Quick Start - Create a working trading project with MetaTrader 4 and CSharpMT4 from scratch.

docs.title: Step 0: Obtain Your API Key
docs.text:
To connect to MetaRPC endpoints (mt4.mrpc.pro:443), obtain your API key:

  1. Register for free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate your API token in your dashboard at https://mrpc.pro/my.
  3. Set your token in your environment or connection config.

docs.title: Step 1: Create Your Project
docs.text:
Create a new directory for your trading bot:

mkdir my_csharpmt4_bot
cd my_csharpmt4_bot

Install the package:

dotnet add package MetaRPC.MT4

docs.title: Step 2: Write Your Trading Code
docs.text:
Create your main application file and paste the following snippet:

using mt4_term_api;
using MetaRPC.MT4;

// Session ID generation on Connect and authentication are handled automatically.
var account = new MT4Account(user, password, grpcServer, apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync(serverName, "EURUSD");   // 3rd arg is a bool (waitForTerminalIsAlive), not a timeout
var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance}, Equity: {summary.AccountEquity}");

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Program
docs.text:
Run your application:

# Verify connection output
# Balance: 10000.00, Equity: 10000.00

docs.title: 🚀 Next Steps
docs.text:
Congratulations! You have successfully established a direct gRPC connection to MetaTrader 4. Next:

  • Explore gRPC Streaming to listen to live ticks.
  • Check the API Reference for all 40+ available terminal methods.
  • Learn about high-level risk management and auto-normalization in MT4Sugar.

docs.title: MT4Service — Account Methods
docs.text:
Account snapshot, statistics and equity history, plus value getters that return a single number/string without re-deriving it from a bulk reply.

→ builds on low-level Account — Overview

docs.title: 📋 Data methods
docs.text: Method Returns Low-level spec AccountSummaryAsync(deadline, ct) AccountSummaryData AccountSummary TradeStatsAsync(from, deadline, ct) StatsData TradeStats TradeUnrealizedPLAsync(from, deadline, ct) TradeUnrealizedPLData TradeUnrealizedPL EquityHistoryAsync(from, excludeSameBars, deadline, ct) EquityHistoryData EquityHistory TradeStatsEquityHistoryAsync(from, excludeSameBars, deadline, ct) StatsWithChartsData TradeStatsEquityHistory

docs.title: 📋 Value getters
docs.text:
All derive from a single AccountSummary round-trip — a readable shortcut, no low-level one-call equivalent.

Method Returns Value GetBalanceAsync(…) double Balance GetEquityAsync(…) double Equity (balance + floating P/L) GetMarginAsync(…) double Used margin GetFreeMarginAsync(…) double Free margin GetMarginLevelAsync(…) double Margin level, percent GetCreditAsync(…) double Credit GetCurrencyAsync(…) string Deposit currency GetAccountNameAsync(…) string Account holder name GetCompanyAsync(…) string Broker / company name

docs.title: 1) One-line status
docs.text:
double balance  = await service.GetBalanceAsync();
double equity   = await service.GetEquityAsync();
string currency = await service.GetCurrencyAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {balance:F2} {currency}, Equity: {equity:F2}");

docs.title: 2) Full snapshot when you need many fields
docs.text:
// Prefer one AccountSummary over many getters if you need several values
var s = await service.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"#{s.AccountLogin} {s.AccountCurrency} Bal={s.AccountBalance} Eq={s.AccountEquity} " +
                  $"Margin={s.AccountMargin} Free={s.AccountMarginFree} Lev=1:{s.AccountLeverage}");

docs.title: 3) Performance read + equity curve
docs.text:
var stats = (await service.TradeStatsAsync()).Summary;
Console.WriteLine($"open={stats?.OpenTrades} openProfit={stats?.OpenProfit} total={stats?.TotalProfit}");

var eq = await service.EquityHistoryAsync();            // can be large — summarize
Console.WriteLine($"{eq.Points.Count} equity point(s)");

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Getter vs snapshot. For one value, a getter is clearest; for several, call AccountSummaryAsync once.
  • Big reads. EquityHistory / TradeStatsEquityHistory can be large — use from / excludeSameBars and print counts, not the whole object.
  • Snapshot semantics. Equity / OpenProfit are live — re-query right before risk decisions.
  • Currency discipline. Money fields are in the account deposit currency.

docs.title: MT4Service — Mid-Level API Overview
docs.text: Not just a wrapper. MT4Service is the typed, data-returning facade over the low-level MT4Account: it forwards the data calls 1:1 and adds convenience getters that have no single low-level equivalent.

docs.title: 🎯 Where it sits
docs.text:
MT4Account (low-level)  →  raw gRPC: build a Request, read Reply.Data
     ↓
MT4Service (mid-level)  →  forwards data methods 1:1 + convenience getters   ← YOU ARE HERE
     ↓
MT4Sugar  (high-level)  →  snapshots, risk sizing, bulk ops (extension methods on MT4Service)

What the mid-level adds:

  • ✅ A single, stable, typed entry point the whole app (and the Sugar layer) builds on.
  • ✅ Convenience getters — GetBalanceAsync, GetDigitsAsync, GetSpreadAsync (computed) — one call instead of re-deriving from a bulk reply.
  • ✅ Same objects as low-level for the 1:1 wrappers, so you can drop down to MT4Account any time.
// Low-level: fetch the quote, then compute spread yourself
var q  = await account.QuoteAsync("EURUSD");
var pt = Math.Pow(10, -(int)(await account.SymbolParamsManyAsync("EURUSD")).SymbolInfos[0].Digits);
var spreadPts = (q.Ask - q.Bid) / pt;

// Mid-level: one call
var spreadPts2 = await service.GetSpreadAsync("EURUSD");

docs.title: 📂 Method groups
docs.text: Group What's inside Account Methods Snapshot, statistics, equity history + value getters (balance/equity/margin/…). Symbol Methods Quotes, symbols, history/bars, tick values, Market Watch + value getters (digits/point/spread/…). Orders Methods Open orders, tickets, order history. Trading Methods Send / modify / close / close-by. Streaming Methods Live ticks, trade events, profit & ticket snapshots, connection state.

docs.title: 🔌 Connection
docs.text:
Setup lives on the service too (it forwards to MT4Account):

await service.ConnectByServerNameAsync("EGlobal-Demo", baseChartSymbol: "EURUSD");
// ...or: await service.ConnectByHostPortAsync("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443, "EURUSD");
var id = await service.GetIdAsync();      // terminal session GUID (usually not needed)
await service.DisconnectAsync();
Method Returns Notes ConnectByServerNameAsync(serverName, baseChartSymbol, waitForTerminalIsAlive, timeoutSeconds, …) Task Primary connect path. ConnectByHostPortAsync(host, port, baseChartSymbol, …) Task Optional host:port fallback. GetIdAsync(ct) Task<Guid> Terminal session id (auto-attached after connect). DisconnectAsync(delete = false) Task Disconnect (optionally delete the instance).

docs.title: 🔗 Usage pattern
docs.text:
• Request/Reply: var data = await service.MethodAsync(args); → returns the typed *Data object.
  • Streaming: await foreach (var x in service.OnMethodAsync(args, ct)) { … }.
  • Timestamps are UTC; failures throw ApiExceptionMT4 (transient gRPC errors are retried with reconnection).

For the full Request/Reply shapes, fields and enums behind any method, follow the spec links in each group into the low-level MT4Account docs.

docs.title: MT4Service — Orders Methods
docs.text:
Read the current order book and history. (Placing/closing orders lives in Trading Methods.)

→ builds on low-level Orders — Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Low-level spec OpenedOrdersAsync(sortType, deadline, ct) OpenedOrdersData OpenedOrders OpenedOrdersTicketsAsync(deadline, ct) OpenedOrdersTicketsData OpenedOrderTickets OrdersHistoryAsync(from, to, sortType, page, itemsPerPage, …) OrdersHistoryData OrdersHistory
  • sortType on OpenedOrdersAsync is EnumOpenedOrderSortType (default SortByOpenTimeAsc).
  • sortType on OrdersHistoryAsync is EnumOrderHistorySortType (default HistorySortByCloseTimeDesc).
  • Each open order's .OrderType is an OpenedOrderType (OoOpBuy/OoOpSell/OoOpBuylimit/…).

docs.title: 1) Monitor the open book
docs.text:
var opened = await service.OpenedOrdersAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"{opened.OrderInfos.Count} open order(s)");
foreach (var o in opened.OrderInfos)
    Console.WriteLine($"[{o.OrderType}] #{o.Ticket} {o.Symbol} {o.Lots}@{o.OpenPrice} P/L={o.Profit}");

docs.title: 3) Last week's closed orders (paged)
docs.text:
var hist = await service.OrdersHistoryAsync(
    DateTime.UtcNow.AddDays(-7), DateTime.UtcNow,
    itemsPerPage: 100);
Console.WriteLine($"{hist.OrdersInfo.Count} closed order(s)");

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Fetch before you act. Re-query right before modify/close to avoid stale-ticket errors.
  • Page long histories. Use page / itemsPerPage for wide ranges.
  • Tickets are int. Store as int (or validate a long fits) before passing to close/modify.

docs.title: MT4Service — Streaming Methods
docs.text:
Real-time server streams. All return IAsyncEnumerable<...> — consume with await foreach and always pass a CancellationToken.

→ builds on low-level Streaming — Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text: Method Yields Low-level spec OnSymbolTickAsync(symbols, ct) OnSymbolTickData RealTimeQuotes OnTradeAsync(ct) OnTradeData TradeUpdates OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync(intervalMs = 1000, ct) OnOpenedOrdersProfitData OrderProfits OnOpenedOrdersTicketsAsync(intervalMs = 1000, ct) OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData OrderTickets OnConnectStateAsync(ct) ConnectStateData ConnectState

docs.title: 1) Live ticks (stop after first)
docs.text:
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
await foreach (var t in service.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{t.SymbolTick?.Bid}/{t.SymbolTick?.Ask}");
    break;
}

docs.title: 2) Floating-P/L monitor (polling interval)
docs.text:
await foreach (var upd in service.OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync(1000, ct))
{
    foreach (var o in upd.OpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdated)
        Console.WriteLine($"#{o.Ticket} {o.Symbol} P/L={o.OrderProfit}");
    Console.WriteLine($"Equity={upd.AccountInfo?.Equity}");
}

docs.title: 3) Connection heartbeat
docs.text:
await foreach (var s in service.OnConnectStateAsync(ct))
    Console.WriteLine($"[{s.State}] connected={s.IsConnected} alive={s.IsAlive} api={s.ApiIsAlive}");

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Always bound the stream. Pass a CancellationToken / timeout; cancellation completes the stream gracefully (a Cancelled status is normal).
  • Snapshot semantics. Profit/ticket streams emit the current set each interval — compute diffs client-side if you need add/remove events.
  • Reconnect. Transient gRPC errors are retried with backoff by the client's stream wrapper.
  • Interval. For the polling streams, 500–2000 ms is typical; faster increases load.

docs.title: MT4Service — Symbol Methods
docs.text:
Quotes, symbol inventory, history/bars, tick values and Market Watch, plus value getters for the common single properties.

→ builds on low-level Market Info — Overview

docs.title: 📋 Data methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Low-level spec SymbolsAsync(deadline, ct) SymbolsData AllSymbols SymbolParamsManyAsync(symbol, deadline, ct) SymbolParamsManyData SymbolParams QuoteAsync(symbol, deadline, ct) QuoteData Quote QuoteManyAsync(symbols, deadline, ct) QuoteManyData QuotesMany QuoteHistoryAsync(symbol, timeframe, from, to, …) QuoteHistoryData QuoteHistory BarsAsync(symbol, timeframe, fromUtc, toUtc, …) QuoteHistoryBarsData Bars TickValueWithSizeAsync(symbols, deadline, ct) TickValueWithSizeData TickValues SymbolSelectAsync(symbol, select = true, …) SymbolSelectData SymbolSelect ServerTimezoneAsync(deadline, ct) ServerTimezoneData ServerTimezone

QuoteHistoryAsync takes ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME (Qh*); BarsAsync takes QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME (Qhb*) — don't mix the two enums.

docs.title: 📋 Value getters
docs.text: Method Returns Value GetDigitsAsync(symbol, …) int Price digits (from SymbolParams) GetPointAsync(symbol, …) double Point size 10^-digits GetSpreadAsync(symbol, …) double Spread in points, computed (Ask-Bid)/point GetBidAsync(symbol, …) double Current bid GetAskAsync(symbol, …) double Current ask GetVolumeMinAsync(symbol, …) double Minimum volume (lots) GetVolumeMaxAsync(symbol, …) double Maximum volume (lots) GetVolumeStepAsync(symbol, …) double Volume step (lots)

docs.title: 1) Price + spread in one glance
docs.text:
var q = await service.QuoteAsync("EURUSD");
Console.WriteLine($"{q.Symbol}: {q.Bid}/{q.Ask}  spread={await service.GetSpreadAsync("EURUSD"):F1}pt");

docs.title: 2) Validate before trading
docs.text:
int    digits = await service.GetDigitsAsync("EURUSD");
double step   = await service.GetVolumeStepAsync("EURUSD");
double min    = await service.GetVolumeMinAsync("EURUSD");
// round price to `digits`, snap volume to `step`, clamp to `min` before OrderSend

docs.title: 3) Candles for a chart
docs.text:
var bars = await service.BarsAsync(
    "EURUSD", QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QhbPeriodH1,
    DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(-6), DateTime.UtcNow);
Console.WriteLine($"{bars.Bars.Count} bar(s)");

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Exact symbol names. Use names from SymbolsAsync() — brokers add suffixes (EURUSD.r).
  • Spread is derived. GetSpreadAsync computes from a live quote; SpreadFloat in symbol params is a flag, not a value.
  • Batch where possible. Prefer QuoteManyAsync / TickValueWithSizeAsync over many single calls.

docs.title: MT4Service — Trading Methods
docs.text:
Place, modify and close orders. These build an explicit request object; for one-liners (market buy/sell, SL/TP in points, risk sizing, bulk close) use MT4Sugar.

→ builds on low-level Orders — Overview

⚠️ These send real orders — guard them in examples/strategies.

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Low-level spec OrderSendAsync(OrderSendRequest request, …) OrderSendData OrderSend OrderModifyAsync(OrderModifyRequest request, …) OrderModifyData OrderModify OrderCloseDeleteAsync(OrderCloseDeleteRequest request, …) OrderCloseDeleteData CloseOrder OrderCloseByAsync(OrderCloseByRequest request, …) OrderCloseByData CloseByOrder
  • OrderSendRequest.OperationType is OrderSendOperationType — OcOpBuy/OcOpSell (market) or OcOpBuylimit/OcOpBuystop/OcOpSelllimit/OcOpSellstop (pending).
  • OrderCloseDeleteData.Mode is OrderCloseDeleteMode (OcdMarketOrder closed / OcdPendingOrder deleted).

docs.title: 1) Market BUY
docs.text:
var sent = await service.OrderSendAsync(new OrderSendRequest {
    Symbol = "EURUSD", OperationType = OrderSendOperationType.OcOpBuy,
    Volume = 0.10, Slippage = 5, Comment = "demo"
});
Console.WriteLine($"opened #{sent.Ticket} @ {sent.Price}");

docs.title: 2) Pending BUY LIMIT
docs.text:
await service.OrderSendAsync(new OrderSendRequest {
    Symbol = "EURUSD", OperationType = OrderSendOperationType.OcOpBuylimit,
    Volume = 0.10, Price = 1.10500, Slippage = 5
});

docs.title: 3) Modify SL/TP, then close
docs.text:
await service.OrderModifyAsync(new OrderModifyRequest {
    OrderTicket = sent.Ticket, NewStopLoss = 1.09500, NewTakeProfit = 1.10500 });

var res = await service.OrderCloseDeleteAsync(new OrderCloseDeleteRequest { OrderTicket = sent.Ticket });
Console.WriteLine($"{res.Mode}: {res.HistoryOrderComment}");

docs.title: 4) Close one order by an opposite one (hedged accounts)
🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Normalize first. Round price to GetDigitsAsync, snap volume to GetVolumeStepAsync, respect GetVolumeMinAsync.
  • Stops distance. Brokers enforce a minimum SL/TP distance; too-tight stops are rejected.
  • Prefer Sugar for common cases. BuyMarketAsync, BuyMarketPointsAsync, ModifySlTpAsync, CloseAllMarketAsync, BuyMarketByRiskAsync build these requests for you.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — High-Level API (with examples)
docs.text: One page, every helper — with a usage example for each. MT4Sugar is a set of extension methods on MT4Service: snapshots, normalization, risk sizing, one-line market orders and bulk close. For the terse machine-generated signature list see the generated index.

docs.title: 🧭 Where it sits
docs.text:
MT4Account (low-level)  →  raw gRPC
     ↓
MT4Service (mid-level)  →  typed facade + getters
     ↓
MT4Sugar  (high-level)  →  convenience extension methods on MT4Service   ← YOU ARE HERE

Because they are extension methods, you call them on a connected service instance (svc below is an MT4Service):

var svc  = new MT4Service(account);                 // account is a connected MT4Account
var snap = await svc.GetAccountSnapshotAsync();

MT4Sugar is intentionally bounded to MT4: no Market Depth/DOM, no OrderCheck/margin helpers, and it works with orders (not netted positions). Signatures below omit the implicit this MT4Service svc receiver. Every method takes optional DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default at the end (shown as …).

docs.title: DTOs
docs.text: Compact value objects returned by the snapshot helpers.

docs.title: AccountSnapshot
docs.text: Field Type Description Login long Account login. Balance double Balance. Equity double Equity (balance + floating P/L). Margin double Used margin. FreeMargin double Free margin. MarginLevel double Margin level, percent. Currency string Deposit currency.

docs.title: SymbolSnapshot
docs.text: Field Type Description Symbol string Symbol name. Bid / Ask double Top of book. Digits int Price digits. Point double Point size (10^-digits). SpreadPoints double Spread in points. VolumeMin / VolumeMax / VolumeStep double Volume limits (lots).

docs.title: GetAccountSnapshotAsync(…)
docs.text:
Pulls the whole money side of the account in one AccountSummary round trip and packs it into an AccountSnapshot. Use it when you want balance/equity/margin together without several getter calls.

var acc = await svc.GetAccountSnapshotAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"{acc.Equity} {acc.Currency} (free margin {acc.FreeMargin})");
if (acc.MarginLevel < 200) Console.WriteLine("margin getting tight");

docs.title: GetSymbolSnapshotAsync(string symbol, …)
docs.text:
Quote plus the contract facts you need to trade the symbol — digits, point, spread, volume limits — in one SymbolSnapshot. The starting point for most sizing/pricing logic.

var s = await svc.GetSymbolSnapshotAsync("EURUSD");
Console.WriteLine($"bid={s.Bid} ask={s.Ask} spread={s.SpreadPoints}pt step={s.VolumeStep}");

docs.title: EnsureSelectedAsync(string symbol, …)
docs.text:
Makes sure the symbol is in Market Watch (SymbolSelect with select: true) so quotes/history are available. Call it once before working with a symbol you're not sure is selected.

await svc.EnsureSelectedAsync("GBPUSD");   // now safe to quote / stream it

docs.title: NormalizePriceAsync(string symbol, double price, …)
docs.text:
Rounds a price to the symbol's Digits. Brokers reject prices off the tick grid, so normalize any computed SL/TP/entry before sending.

double sl = await svc.NormalizePriceAsync("EURUSD", rawSl);   // e.g. 1.094827 → 1.09483

docs.title: NormalizeVolumeAsync(string symbol, double volume, …)
docs.text:
Clamps a volume into [VolumeMin … VolumeMax] and snaps it onto VolumeStep. Prevents "invalid volume" rejections from hand-computed lot sizes.

double vol = await svc.NormalizeVolumeAsync("EURUSD", 0.023);  // → 0.02 on a 0.01 step

docs.title: PointsToPipsAsync(string symbol, double points, …)
docs.text:
Converts points to pips (on 3/5-digit symbols 1 pip = 10 points). Handy for display, since humans think in pips but the API works in points.

double pips = await svc.PointsToPipsAsync("EURUSD", 200);   // → 20

docs.title: PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync(string symbol, bool fromAsk, double offsetPoints, …)
docs.text:
Returns a normalized absolute price a given number of points away from the current Ask (fromAsk: true) or Bid. Negative offset goes below. The building block for SL/TP and pending-order levels.

// take-profit 300 points above Ask; stop 150 points below Ask
double tp = await svc.PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync("EURUSD", fromAsk: true, offsetPoints:  300);
double sl = await svc.PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync("EURUSD", fromAsk: true, offsetPoints: -150);

docs.title: OrdersHistoryLastAsync(TimeSpan window, …)
docs.text:
Closed-order history for the last window up to now — a shortcut over the dated OrdersHistory call.

var hist = await svc.OrdersHistoryLastAsync(TimeSpan.FromDays(7));
Console.WriteLine($"{hist.OrdersInfo.Count} orders closed this week");

docs.title: GetOrderCountAsync(string? symbol = null, …)
docs.text:
How many orders are open — overall, or for one symbol when you pass it.

int all = await svc.GetOrderCountAsync();
int eur = await svc.GetOrderCountAsync("EURUSD");

docs.title: GetTotalProfitLossAsync(string? symbol = null, …)
docs.text:
Total floating P/L of open orders (optionally one symbol). The usual input to a safety cap.

if (await svc.GetTotalProfitLossAsync() < -100) Console.WriteLine("stand down");

docs.title: TotalLotsAsync(string? symbol = null, …)
docs.text:
Total open volume in lots (optionally one symbol) — a quick exposure gauge.

double lots = await svc.TotalLotsAsync("EURUSD");

docs.title: GetOrdersBySymbolAsync(string symbol, …)
docs.text:
All open orders on one symbol, as a list you can iterate.

foreach (var o in await svc.GetOrdersBySymbolAsync("EURUSD"))
    Console.WriteLine($"#{o.Ticket} {o.OrderType} {o.Lots}@{o.OpenPrice} P/L={o.Profit}");

docs.title: GetOrderByTicketAsync(long ticket, …)
docs.text:
Looks up one open order by ticket, or null if it isn't open.

var o = await svc.GetOrderByTicketAsync(12345678);
if (o is null) Console.WriteLine("not open (closed or wrong ticket)");

docs.title: GetProfitableOrdersAsync(string? symbol = null, …) / GetLosingOrdersAsync(string? symbol = null, …)
docs.text:
The open book split into winners and losers — e.g. to close only the losing side.

var losers  = await svc.GetLosingOrdersAsync("EURUSD");
var winners = await svc.GetProfitableOrdersAsync("EURUSD");
Console.WriteLine($"{winners.Count} up / {losers.Count} down");

docs.title: GetLastClosedOrderAsync(TimeSpan window, …)
docs.text:
The single most recent closed order within window, or null.

var last = await svc.GetLastClosedOrderAsync(TimeSpan.FromDays(1));
Console.WriteLine(last is null ? "nothing closed today" : $"last #{last.Ticket}");

docs.title: 4. Trading
docs.text:
→ builds on MT4Service · Trading

⚠️ All trading helpers place real orders. Guard them behind a flag in examples/strategies.

docs.title: BuyMarketAsync(string symbol, double volume, double? sl = null, double? tp = null, int slippage = 5, int magic = 0, string comment = "MT4Sugar", …) / SellMarketAsync(…)
docs.text:
Market order with absolute SL/TP prices; volume is auto-normalized, price is the current Ask (buy) / Bid (sell).

var r = await svc.BuyMarketAsync("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: 1.0950, tp: 1.1050);
Console.WriteLine($"opened #{r.Ticket} @ {r.Price}");

docs.title: BuyMarketPointsAsync(string symbol, double volume, double? slPoints = null, double? tpPoints = null, …) / SellMarketPointsAsync(…)
docs.text:
Same, but SL/TP are given in points from the fill price — no need to compute absolute levels yourself.

// buy 0.10 lot, stop 150 points away, target 300 points away
await svc.BuyMarketPointsAsync("EURUSD", 0.10, slPoints: 150, tpPoints: 300);

docs.title: ModifySlTpAsync(int ticket, double? sl = null, double? tp = null, …)
docs.text:
Changes an order's SL/TP (absolute prices). Pass only what you want to change — null leaves a field as-is. This is how trailing/break-even logic moves stops.

await svc.ModifySlTpAsync(12345678, tp: 1.1075);        // set/raise TP, leave SL
await svc.ModifySlTpAsync(12345678, sl: newTrailStop);  // ratchet the stop

docs.title: CloseByTicketAsync(int ticket, …)
docs.text:
Closes a market order, or deletes a pending order, by ticket.

await svc.CloseByTicketAsync(12345678);

docs.title: CloseAllAsync(string? symbol = null, …)
docs.text:
Closes/deletes every open order (optionally just one symbol); returns how many it acted on. The "flatten everything" button.

int n = await svc.CloseAllAsync();              // whole account
int e = await svc.CloseAllAsync("EURUSD");      // just EURUSD

docs.title: CloseAllMarketAsync(string? symbol = null, …) / CancelAllPendingAsync(string? symbol = null, …)
docs.text:
The two halves of CloseAll: close only market positions, or delete only pending orders. Returns the count.

await svc.CloseAllMarketAsync("EURUSD");    // flatten positions, keep pendings
await svc.CancelAllPendingAsync("EURUSD");  // clear pendings, keep positions

docs.title: CalcVolumeForRiskAsync(string symbol, double stopPoints, double riskMoney, …)
docs.text:
Sizes a position so a stopPoints move against you costs exactly riskMoney. Reads tick value internally and returns a broker-valid (normalized) volume. The heart of risk-based entries.

// how many lots make a 200-point stop cost $50?
double vol = await svc.CalcVolumeForRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50);

docs.title: BuyMarketByRiskAsync(string symbol, double stopPoints, double riskMoney, int slippage = 5, int magic = 0, string comment = "MT4Sugar", …) / SellMarketByRiskAsync(…)
docs.text:
One call that sizes by risk and opens the order with its protective stop already attached (stopPoints below Ask for buy / above Bid for sell). The safest way to enter — you're never left without an SL.

// risk $50 over a 200-point stop; volume is computed and the SL is placed for you
var r = await svc.BuyMarketByRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50);
Console.WriteLine($"opened #{r.Ticket} vol={r.Volume} @ {r.Price}");

docs.title: ReadTicks(string symbol, CancellationToken ct = default)
docs.text:
Live tick stream for one symbol as IAsyncEnumerable — consume with await foreach, stop via the token. (See gRPC Streaming.)

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
try { await foreach (var t in svc.ReadTicks("EURUSD", cts.Token))
          Console.WriteLine($"{t.SymbolTick.Bid}/{t.SymbolTick.Ask}"); }
catch (OperationCanceledException) { }

docs.title: ReadTrades(CancellationToken ct = default)
docs.text:
Live trade-event stream (order create/modify/close), same consumption pattern.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
try { await foreach (var ev in svc.ReadTrades(cts.Token)) Console.WriteLine(ev); }
catch (OperationCanceledException) { }

Tip: a sugar method is just a readable shortcut over MT4Service. For the underlying Request/Reply shapes and fields, follow the group link to MT4Service, then its spec into the MT4Account low-level docs. For the terse signature list, see the generated index.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetAccountSnapshotAsync
docs.text:
A compact account snapshot from a single AccountSummary round-trip.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Pulls the whole money side of the account in one AccountSummary round trip and packs it into an AccountSnapshot, so you get balance, equity, margin and currency together instead of several getter calls. A natural first step before deciding whether to trade.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<AccountSnapshot> GetAccountSnapshotAsync(DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
AccountSnapshot — a compact value object:

Field Type Meaning Login long Account login. Balance double Balance. Equity double Equity (balance + floating P/L). Margin double Used margin. FreeMargin double Free margin available for new trades. MarginLevel double Margin level, percent. Currency string Deposit currency.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
var a = await svc.GetAccountSnapshotAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"#{a.Login} {a.Currency} Bal={a.Balance} Eq={a.Equity} Free={a.FreeMargin}");

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Gate trading on account health before sending any order.

var a = await svc.GetAccountSnapshotAsync();
if (a.FreeMargin < 500 || a.MarginLevel < 200)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Low margin (free={a.FreeMargin}, level={a.MarginLevel}%) — skip entry.");
    return;
}
Console.WriteLine($"OK to trade: equity {a.Equity} {a.Currency}");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• One round trip. Cheaper than calling GetBalance/GetEquity/… separately.
  • Gate risk with it. FreeMargin / MarginLevel make a good pre-trade safety check.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• GetSymbolSnapshotAsync — the symbol-side counterpart.
  • MT4Sugar overview · MT4Service · Account

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetSymbolSnapshotAsync
docs.text:
Top-of-book price plus the contract facts you need to trade a symbol — digits, point, spread and volume limits — in one object.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Reads the symbol once and bundles everything a sizing/pricing decision needs into a single SymbolSnapshot: the live quote (Bid/Ask), the price precision (Digits/Point), the current SpreadPoints, and the tradable volume limits. It saves you from calling QuoteAsync plus several Get* getters and stitching the results together yourself. Use it as the first step of almost any trade: read the snapshot, then size and price from its fields.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<SymbolSnapshot> GetSymbolSnapshotAsync(string symbol, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument to read, e.g. "EURUSD". deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying calls. ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
SymbolSnapshot — a compact value object:

Field Type Meaning Symbol string The symbol name. Bid / Ask double Current top-of-book prices. Digits int Price decimal places. Point double Point size, 10^-Digits (e.g. 0.00001 on 5 digits). SpreadPoints double Current spread in points ((Ask − Bid) / Point). VolumeMin / VolumeMax double Smallest / largest tradable volume (lots). VolumeStep double Volume increment (lots).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
var s = await svc.GetSymbolSnapshotAsync("EURUSD");
Console.WriteLine($"{s.Symbol} {s.Bid}/{s.Ask} digits={s.Digits} spread={s.SpreadPoints}pt vol[{s.VolumeMin}..{s.VolumeMax}/{s.VolumeStep}]");

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Read the symbol once, then use its fields to filter and price an entry.

var s = await svc.GetSymbolSnapshotAsync("EURUSD");

// 1) skip trading when the spread is abnormally wide
if (s.SpreadPoints > 25) { Console.WriteLine($"spread {s.SpreadPoints}pt too wide — skip"); return; }

// 2) price a 150-point stop off the snapshot, then enter at the minimum lot
double sl = s.Ask - 150 * s.Point;
await svc.BuyMarketAsync(s.Symbol, s.VolumeMin, sl: sl);

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Select first. If the symbol isn't in Market Watch the quote may be empty — call EnsureSelectedAsync once beforehand.
  • Point vs pip. Point is the raw price step; on 3/5-digit symbols 1 pip = 10 points (see PointsToPipsAsync).
  • Snapshot, not a stream. It's a one-shot read; for live updates use ReadTicks.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• GetAccountSnapshotAsync — the account-side counterpart.
  • NormalizeVolumeAsync · PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync — size and price from these fields.
  • MT4Sugar overview · MT4Service · Symbol

docs.title: MT4Sugar · EnsureSelectedAsync
docs.text:
Ensure the symbol is in Market Watch (SymbolSelect with select=true) before quoting/trading.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Makes sure the symbol is present in Market Watch (calls SymbolSelect with select: true). A symbol that isn't selected may return empty quotes and can't be streamed, so call this once before working with an unfamiliar symbol.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task EnsureSelectedAsync(string symbol, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Task — completes once the symbol is selected.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
A symbol not in Market Watch returns no quotes — select it first.

await svc.EnsureSelectedAsync("GBPJPY");
var q = await svc.QuoteAsync("GBPJPY");   // now returns a live quote
Console.WriteLine($"GBPJPY {q.Bid}/{q.Ask}");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Idempotent. Selecting an already-selected symbol is harmless.
  • Do it first. Quotes/streams for an unselected symbol can come back empty.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• GetSymbolSnapshotAsync — read the symbol after selecting it.
  • MT4Sugar overview · MT4Service · Symbol

docs.title: MT4Sugar · NormalizePriceAsync
docs.text:
Round a raw price to the symbol's digits.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Rounds a price to the symbol's Digits. Brokers reject prices that don't sit on the tick grid, so run any computed entry/SL/TP through this before sending it.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<double> NormalizePriceAsync(string symbol, double price, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". price double — The price to round. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: double — the price rounded to the symbol's digits.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Compute a stop, then round it to the tick grid before modifying — brokers reject off-tick prices.

double rawSl = entry - 150 * point;                 // may land between ticks
double sl   = await svc.NormalizePriceAsync("EURUSD", rawSl);
await svc.ModifySlTpAsync(ticket, sl: sl);

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Prevents invalid price rejections from arithmetic that lands between ticks.
  • Pair with NormalizeVolumeAsync to validate the other half of an order.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync — already returns a normalized price.
  • MT4Sugar overview · MT4Service · Symbol

docs.title: MT4Sugar · NormalizeVolumeAsync
docs.text:
Clamp & snap a raw volume to the symbol's min/max/step → a broker-valid lot size.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Clamps a volume into [VolumeMin … VolumeMax] and snaps it onto VolumeStep. Hand-computed lot sizes rarely land on a valid step, so normalize before ordering.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<double> NormalizeVolumeAsync(string symbol, double volume, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". volume double — The raw volume (lots) to clamp and snap. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
A lot from a sizing formula is rarely on the broker's step — snap it before ordering.

double raw = equity * 0.01 / 1000;                  // e.g. 0.237
double vol = await svc.NormalizeVolumeAsync("EURUSD", raw);   // -> 0.23 on a 0.01 step
await svc.BuyMarketAsync("EURUSD", vol);

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Prevents invalid volume rejections.
  • The by-risk and market helpers already normalize internally — use this when you build the order yourself.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• CalcVolumeForRiskAsync — produces an already-normalized volume.
  • MT4Sugar overview · MT4Service · Symbol

docs.title: MT4Sugar · PointsToPipsAsync
docs.text:
Convert points to pips (on 3/5-digit symbols 1 pip = 10 points).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Converts a distance in points to pips. On 3/5-digit symbols 1 pip = 10 points; on 2/4-digit symbols they're equal. Handy for display, since the API works in points but humans think in pips.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<double> PointsToPipsAsync(string symbol, double points, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". points double — A distance in points to convert. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: double — the same distance expressed in pips.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Work in points internally, show the trader pips.

double stopPoints = 200;
double pips = await svc.PointsToPipsAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints);
Console.WriteLine($"stop = {stopPoints} points ({pips} pips)");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Display only. All order/price math stays in points.
  • Point itself comes from GetSymbolSnapshotAsync.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync — turns points into an absolute price.
  • MT4Sugar overview · MT4Service · Symbol

docs.title: MT4Sugar · PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync
docs.text:
A normalized price at offsetPoints from Ask (fromAsk:true) or Bid; offset may be negative.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Returns a normalized absolute price a given number of points away from the current Ask (fromAsk: true) or Bid. Negative offset goes below the market. The building block for SL/TP levels and pending-order prices.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<double> PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync(string symbol, bool fromAsk, double offsetPoints, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". fromAsk bool — true = measure from Ask, false = from Bid. offsetPoints double — Signed distance in points; negative goes below. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: double sl = await svc.PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync("EURUSD", fromAsk: true, offsetPoints: -200);

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Build absolute SL/TP around the market, then open the order with them.

double sl = await svc.PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync("EURUSD", fromAsk: true, offsetPoints: -150);
double tp = await svc.PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync("EURUSD", fromAsk: true, offsetPoints:  300);
await svc.BuyMarketAsync("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: sl, tp: tp);

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Already normalized — no extra NormalizePrice needed.
  • Buy stops/targets usually measure from Ask; sell stops/targets from Bid.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetLastClosedOrderAsync
docs.text:
The most recent closed order within window, or null.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: The single most recent closed order within window, or null. Handy for a cooldown — don't re-enter right after the previous trade closed.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<HistoryOrderInfo?> GetLastClosedOrderAsync(TimeSpan window, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning window TimeSpan — Look-back period ending now. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: HistoryOrderInfo? — the order, or null if nothing closed in the window. Exposes .Ticket.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Cooldown: don't re-enter right after the previous trade closed.

var last = await svc.GetLastClosedOrderAsync(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5));
if (last != null) { Console.WriteLine($"traded recently (#{last.Ticket}) — wait"); return; }

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • For the full list of recent closes, use OrdersHistoryLastAsync.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetLosingOrdersAsync
docs.text:
Open orders currently at a loss (optionally one symbol).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: The open orders currently at a loss (optionally one symbol) — e.g. to cut losers while letting winners run.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<List<OpenedOrderInfo>> GetLosingOrdersAsync(string? symbol = null, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string? null Restrict to one symbol, or null for the whole account. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Cut losers: close only the orders currently at a loss, keep the winners running.

foreach (var o in await svc.GetLosingOrdersAsync("EURUSD"))
    await svc.CloseByTicketAsync((int)o.Ticket);

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetOrderByTicketAsync
docs.text:
Find an open order by ticket, or null.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Looks up a single open order by its ticket, or null if it isn't open (closed, or wrong ticket). Use it to confirm an order still exists before acting on it.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<OpenedOrderInfo?> GetOrderByTicketAsync(long ticket, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning ticket long — Order ticket. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: OpenedOrderInfo? — the order, or null. Each item exposes Ticket, OrderType, Lots, OpenPrice, Profit.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
var o = await svc.GetOrderByTicketAsync(462208455);
if (o is not null) Console.WriteLine($"{o.Symbol} P/L={o.Profit}");

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Confirm an order is still open before acting on it.

var o = await svc.GetOrderByTicketAsync(ticket);
if (o is null) { Console.WriteLine("already closed"); return; }
await svc.ModifySlTpAsync(ticket, tp: o.OpenPrice + 300 * point);

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • null is normal when the order has already closed — handle it before modify/close.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetOrderCountAsync
docs.text:
Number of open orders (optionally for one symbol).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: How many orders are currently open — account-wide, or for one symbol when you pass it. Useful to cap concurrency.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<int> GetOrderCountAsync(string? symbol = null, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string? null Restrict to one symbol, or null for the whole account. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
int n = await svc.GetOrderCountAsync();           // all
int e = await svc.GetOrderCountAsync("EURUSD");   // one symbol

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Cap concurrency: don't open more than N orders at once.

if (await svc.GetOrderCountAsync("EURUSD") >= 3)
{
    Console.WriteLine("already 3 EURUSD orders — skip");
    return;
}
await svc.BuyMarketByRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50);

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • Counts open orders (market + pending). For lots, use TotalLotsAsync.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetOrdersBySymbolAsync
docs.text:
All open orders for a symbol.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: All open orders on one symbol, as a list you can iterate — e.g. to inspect before flattening it.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<List<OpenedOrderInfo>> GetOrdersBySymbolAsync(string symbol, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: List<OpenedOrderInfo> — open orders on the symbol. Each item exposes Ticket, OrderType, Lots, OpenPrice, Profit.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
List the open book on one symbol — e.g. before deciding to flatten it.

foreach (var o in await svc.GetOrdersBySymbolAsync("EURUSD"))
    Console.WriteLine($"#{o.Ticket} {o.OrderType} {o.Lots}@{o.OpenPrice} P/L={o.Profit}");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Returns an empty list when nothing is open on the symbol.
  • Filtered variants: GetProfitableOrdersAsync / GetLosingOrdersAsync.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetProfitableOrdersAsync
docs.text:
Open orders currently in profit (optionally one symbol).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: The open orders currently in profit (optionally one symbol) — e.g. to take partial profit by closing only the winners.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<List<OpenedOrderInfo>> GetProfitableOrdersAsync(string? symbol = null, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string? null Restrict to one symbol, or null for the whole account. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Take partial profit: close only the orders currently in the green.

foreach (var o in await svc.GetProfitableOrdersAsync("EURUSD"))
    await svc.CloseByTicketAsync((int)o.Ticket);

docs.title: MT4Sugar · GetTotalProfitLossAsync
docs.text:
Total floating profit of open orders (optionally one symbol).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Total floating P/L across open orders (optionally one symbol). The usual input to a floating-loss safety cap.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<double> GetTotalProfitLossAsync(string? symbol = null, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string? null Restrict to one symbol, or null for the whole account. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: double — summed floating P/L in deposit currency.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Floating-loss safety cap before adding risk (the pattern the Adaptive preset uses).

double floating = await svc.GetTotalProfitLossAsync();
if (floating < -100) { Console.WriteLine($"floating {floating} below cap — stand down"); return; }

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Floating, not realized. For closed trades use OrdersHistoryLastAsync.
  • Negative values are losses — compare against a cap before adding risk.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · OrdersHistoryLastAsync
docs.text:
Order history for the last window up to now.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Closed-order history for the last window up to now — a shortcut over the dated OrdersHistory call when you just want "recent".

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<OrdersHistoryData> OrdersHistoryLastAsync(TimeSpan window, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning window TimeSpan — Look-back period ending now. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: OrdersHistoryData — .OrdersInfo is the list of closed orders in the window.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
End-of-day check: how much closed in the last 24 hours.

var h = await svc.OrdersHistoryLastAsync(TimeSpan.FromDays(1));
Console.WriteLine($"{h.OrdersInfo.Count} order(s) closed in the last day");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Window ends now. Pass e.g. TimeSpan.FromDays(7) for the last week.
  • For just the single most recent close, use GetLastClosedOrderAsync.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · TotalLotsAsync
docs.text:
Total open volume in lots (optionally one symbol).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Total open volume in lots (optionally one symbol) — a quick exposure gauge for position limits.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<double> TotalLotsAsync(string? symbol = null, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string? null Restrict to one symbol, or null for the whole account. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Exposure cap: stop opening once total volume on a symbol is reached.

if (await svc.TotalLotsAsync("EURUSD") >= 1.0) { Console.WriteLine("EURUSD exposure full"); return; }
await svc.BuyMarketAsync("EURUSD", 0.10);

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • Sums all open orders' volume; combine with GetOrderCountAsync for a fuller picture.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · BuyMarketAsync
docs.text:
Market BUY (volume auto-normalized, price = Ask). SL/TP are absolute prices.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Opens a market BUY at the current Ask. Volume is auto-normalized; SL/TP are absolute prices (pass null to omit). Returns the broker reply.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<OrderSendData> BuyMarketAsync(string symbol, double volume, double? sl = null, double? tp = null, int slippage = 5, int magic = 0, string comment = "MT4Sugar", ...)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". volume double — Order volume in lots (auto-normalized to the symbol's step). sl double? null Absolute stop-loss price, or null for none. tp double? null Absolute take-profit price, or null for none. slippage int 5 Max allowed price slippage, in points. magic int 0 Magic-number tag for the order. comment string "MT4Sugar" Order comment. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: OrderSendData — the broker reply. Ticket > 0 means success; it also carries Volume and Price.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Snapshot → size → buy with absolute SL/TP → confirm.

var s  = await svc.GetSymbolSnapshotAsync("EURUSD");
var r  = await svc.BuyMarketAsync("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: s.Bid - 150 * s.Point, tp: s.Ask + 300 * s.Point);
Console.WriteLine(r.Ticket > 0 ? $"opened #{r.Ticket} @ {r.Price}" : "rejected");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• ⚠️ Places a real order — guard it behind a flag in examples/strategies.
  • For SL/TP as point distances use BuyMarketPointsAsync; to size by risk use BuyMarketByRiskAsync.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · BuyMarketPointsAsync
docs.text:
Market BUY with SL/TP expressed in points from Ask.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Market BUY where SL/TP are given as point distances from the fill instead of absolute prices — no need to compute levels yourself.

docs.title: Signature

var orders = await svc.GetOrdersBySymbolAsync("EURUSD");

docs.text:
Modify an order's SL/TP (absolute prices; null leaves a field unchanged).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Changes an order's SL/TP (absolute prices). Pass only what you want to change — null leaves a field untouched. This is how break-even and trailing logic move stops.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<OrderModifyData> ModifySlTpAsync(int ticket, double? sl = null, double? tp = null, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning ticket int — Order ticket. sl double? null Absolute stop-loss price, or null for none. tp double? null Absolute take-profit price, or null for none. deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.text: OrderModifyData — the broker reply for the modify.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Move the stop to break-even once the trade is in profit.

var o = await svc.GetOrderByTicketAsync(ticket);
if (o != null && o.Profit > 0)
    await svc.ModifySlTpAsync(ticket, sl: o.OpenPrice);   // lock in: SL = entry

docs.text:

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Opens a market SELL at the current Bid. Volume is auto-normalized; SL/TP are absolute prices (SL above, TP below). Mirror of BuyMarketAsync.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: One call that sizes by risk and opens a BUY with its protective stop already attached (stopPoints below Ask). The safest way to enter — you're never left without an SL.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<OrderSendData> BuyMarketByRiskAsync(string symbol, double stopPoints, double riskMoney, int slippage = 5, int magic = 0, string comment = "MT4Sugar", ...)

docs.title: Parameters

docs.text:
One call: size by risk AND open with the protective stop attached.

var r = await svc.BuyMarketByRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50);
Console.WriteLine($"opened #{r.Ticket} vol={r.Volume} @ {r.Price}");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• ⚠️ Places a real order — guard it.
  • Combines CalcVolumeForRiskAsync + a market entry with the SL set for you.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · CalcVolumeForRiskAsync
docs.text:
Volume for a fixed money risk over a stop distance (from TickValueWithSize), normalized.

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Sizes a position so that a stopPoints move against you costs exactly riskMoney. Reads tick value internally and returns a broker-valid (normalized) volume. The heart of risk-based entries.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: Task<double> CalcVolumeForRiskAsync(string symbol, double stopPoints, double riskMoney, DateTime? deadline = null, CancellationToken ct = default)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". stopPoints double — Stop distance in points (drives both the sizing and the SL). riskMoney double — Money to lose if the stop is hit (deposit currency). deadline DateTime? null Optional hard deadline for the underlying call(s). ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: double — the risk-sized volume in lots (already normalized).

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Size first, then build your own order with that volume.

double vol = await svc.CalcVolumeForRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 50);
double sl  = await svc.PriceFromOffsetPointsAsync("EURUSD", fromAsk: true, offsetPoints: -200);
await svc.BuyMarketAsync("EURUSD", vol, sl: sl);

docs.text:
• Returns the symbol's min volume when inputs are non-positive or tick value is unavailable.
  • For a one-call sized entry use BuyMarketByRiskAsync / SellMarketByRiskAsync.

docs.title: MT4Sugar · ReadTicks
docs.text:
Live tick stream for a single symbol (thin alias over OnSymbolTickAsync).

→ extension method on MT4Service — Sugar is just a readable shortcut over the service.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Live tick stream for one symbol as an IAsyncEnumerable — consume with await foreach, stop via the CancellationToken. A thin reader over the service's tick subscription.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning symbol string — Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". ct CancellationToken default Cancellation token — your off-switch for the stream.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3));
await foreach (var t in svc.ReadTicks("EURUSD", cts.Token))
    Console.WriteLine($"{t.SymbolTick?.Bid}/{t.SymbolTick?.Ask}");

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Watch price for a few seconds, acting on each tick, then stop via the token.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
try
{
    await foreach (var t in svc.ReadTicks("EURUSD", cts.Token))
        if (t.SymbolTick.Bid > 1.1000) { Console.WriteLine("level hit"); break; }
}
catch (OperationCanceledException) { }

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Cancel to stop. Use a CancellationTokenSource with CancelAfter, and catch OperationCanceledException.
  • Full lifecycle & reconnect behavior: gRPC Streaming.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
try { await foreach (var ev in svc.ReadTrades(cts.Token)) Console.WriteLine($"trade event: {ev}"); }

docs.title: MT4Account — Master Overview
docs.text: One page to orient fast: what lives where, how to choose the right API, and jump links to every group overview and method spec in the low-level (MT4Account) docs set.

docs.title: 🚦 Start here — Group Overviews
docs.text:
Group Account

Snapshot, trade stats, unrealized P/L, equity history.

5 methods Group Market Info

Quotes, symbols, history/bars, tick values, timezone.

9 methods Group Orders

Open orders & history, send / modify / close / close-by.

7 methods Group Streaming

Ticks, trades, profit & ticket snapshots, connect state.

5 methods

📖 Stream management guide — patterns, cancellation, reconnection.

MT4 is intentionally leaner than MT5: no Market Depth (DOM), no OrderCheck/OrderCalcMargin, and it works with orders (not netted positions). Account/symbol values come back as whole-object replies rather than per-property getters.

docs.title: 🧭 How to pick an API
docs.text: If you need… Go to… Typical calls Account snapshot / performance Account AccountSummaryAsync, TradeStatsAsync, EquityHistoryAsync Quotes & symbol properties Market Info QuoteAsync, QuoteManyAsync, SymbolParamsManyAsync, SymbolsAsync History / candles Market Info QuoteHistoryAsync, BarsAsync Sizing inputs (tick value, timezone) Market Info TickValueWithSizeAsync, ServerTimezoneAsync Current orders & history Orders OpenedOrdersAsync, OpenedOrdersTicketsAsync, OrdersHistoryAsync Trading operations Orders OrderSendAsync, OrderModifyAsync, OrderCloseDeleteAsync, OrderCloseByAsync Real-time updates Streaming OnSymbolTickAsync, OnTradeAsync, OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync, OnConnectStateAsync

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (gRPC)
docs.text:
Every data method exists in two versions: Async (recommended) and a Sync twin (rare scenarios).

// Async (recommended)
var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
var quote   = await account.QuoteAsync("EURUSD");

// Sync twin (blocking)
var summary2 = account.AccountSummary();
var quote2   = account.Quote("EURUSD");

Every method follows the same shape:

  • Proto Service/Method: Service.Method(Request) → Reply
  • C# wrapper: await mt4Account.MethodAsync(...) (or the sync Method())
  • Reply payload: Reply.Data (proto-generated object)
  • Errors: failures throw ApiExceptionMT4 (the gateway error is surfaced, not a numeric code); transient gRPC errors are retried with reconnection.

Timestamps are UTC (google.protobuf.Timestamp). Streaming methods return IAsyncEnumerable<T> — consume with await foreach and always pass a CancellationToken.
