docs.text:
Returns OrderCloseDeleteData with:

Field Type Description Mode OrderCloseDeleteMode Whether a market order was closed or a pending deleted — see enum below. HistoryOrderComment string Server comment explaining the result.

docs.title: OrderCloseDeleteMode — field Mode
docs.text:
• OcdMarketOrder = 0 — a market order was closed
  • OcdPendingOrder = 1 — a pending order was deleted

The actual action (close vs delete) is determined by the server based on the order state/type.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Close or delete an order by its ticket — convenient for:

  • Manual trade intervention from UI/debug tools
  • Post-trade cleanup
  • Simulating close workflows in sandbox/testing

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Ticket range. The wire type is int. If you store tickets as long, ensure the value fits into Int32 before sending (the wrapper does this check).
  • State matters. Market positions are typically closed; pending orders are typically deleted — the server sets Mode accordingly.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Invalid/closed ticket. Calling the method for a non-open ticket yields an API error — handle ApiExceptionMT4.
  • Race conditions. Another process might close the ticket between fetching and sending your request; retry logic should be at the caller level if needed.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. Use a fresh open ticket from OpenedOrdersAsync(); verify Mode and that the ticket disappears from the open-orders list.
  • Failure path. Try an obviously invalid ticket and assert that an ApiExceptionMT4 is thrown and logged without crashing.

docs.title: Modifying an Order (SL/TP/Price)
docs.text:
Request: change an existing order's stop-loss, take-profit, price or expiration via OrderModify. Returns whether the modification was accepted.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT4Account.OrderModifyAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderModify (in the TradingHelper service)

            OrderModifyRequest request,
            DateTime? deadline = null,

}

OrderModifyRequest { OrderTicket: int, NewPrice?, NewStopLoss?, NewTakeProfit?, NewExpiration? }

docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (typed, data-returning) ---
// Build the request (see below) and call: await _service.OrderModifyAsync(request);
// Or via sugar (SL/TP only): await _service.ModifySlTpAsync(ticket, sl: 1.0950, tp: 1.1050);

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Preconditions: account is connected via ConnectByServerName/ConnectByHostPort.

{
    OrderTicket   = 123456,
    NewStopLoss   = 1.09500,   // set only the fields you want to change

docs.text:
OrderModifyRequest — fields:

Field Type Required Description OrderTicket int ✔️ Ticket of the order to modify. NewPrice double ➖ New price (for a pending order). NewStopLoss double ➖ New stop-loss price. NewTakeProfit double ➖ New take-profit price. NewExpiration Timestamp ➖ New expiration (for a pending order).

Optional call parameters:

  • deadline (DateTime?) — optional absolute UTC deadline.
  • cancellationToken (CancellationToken) — cooperative cancel.

Only set the fields you intend to change; the Has* flags on the proto track which were supplied.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text: Field Type Description OrderWasModified bool true if the broker accepted the change.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Adjust protective stops or a pending order's price/expiration without closing it:

  • Move SL to breakeven / trail a stop.
  • Attach or retarget a take-profit.
  • Re-price or re-time a pending order.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prices are absolute. Pass broker-valid, normalized prices (see SymbolParams Digits), not offsets.
  • Stops distance. Brokers enforce a minimum stop distance; too-tight SL/TP is rejected.
  • Sugar shortcut. MT4Sugar.ModifySlTpAsync(ticket, sl, tp) builds the request for the common SL/TP case.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Unchanged values. Submitting the current SL/TP unchanged may be rejected as a no-op by some brokers.
  • Wrong ticket/state. Modifying a closed/invalid ticket throws ApiExceptionMT4.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. Open a market order, then set SL/TP a safe distance away → OrderWasModified = true, visible in OpenedOrders.
  • Failure path. Try a stop closer than the broker minimum and confirm a clear handled error.

No required parameters.

Optional:

  • deadline (DateTime?) — optional UTC deadline for the call.
  • cancellationToken (CancellationToken) — optional cancellation token.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text:
Returns OpenedOrdersTicketsData with:

Field Type Description Tickets RepeatedField<int> List of ticket IDs for currently open orders.

Each ticket is an int that uniquely identifies an open trade in MT4.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: Use this when you only need IDs, e.g. for quick matching/sync, or to feed targeted operations like Close/Delete or Close By without fetching full order rows. Minimal bandwidth versus OpenedOrdersAsync().

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Int32 boundary. MT4 tickets are int. If your app stores them as long, ensure values fit into Int32 before sending to close/modify APIs.
  • Empty ≠ error. An empty list simply means there are no open orders right now.
  • Freshness. In volatile markets, fetch tickets right before acting; another process may open/close orders in between.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text: • Race conditions. A ticket can disappear between listing and action; handle ApiExceptionMT4 from subsequent calls (e.g., Ticket not found).

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. Open a small market order; verify its ticket appears in the list.
  • No orders. Close all trades and confirm the method returns an empty Tickets list without errors.

docs.title: Getting Opened Orders
docs.text:
Request: retrieve currently opened orders from MT4 Fetch all active (non‑closed) trade positions on the account.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT4Account.OpenedOrdersAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OpenedOrders (in the AccountHelper service)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OpenedOrders(OpenedOrdersRequest) → OpenedOrdersReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): AccountHelper.AccountHelperClient.OpenedOrders(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace mt4_term_api
{
    public class MT4Account
    {
        public async Task<OpenedOrdersData> OpenedOrdersAsync(
            EnumOpenedOrderSortType sortType = EnumOpenedOrderSortType.SortByOpenTimeAsc,
            DateTime? deadline = null,
            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    }
}

Request message:

OpenedOrdersRequest { sortType: EnumOpenedOrderSortType }

Reply message:

OpenedOrdersReply { data: OpenedOrdersData }

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (typed, data-returning) ---
var opened = await _service.OpenedOrdersAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"{opened.OrderInfos.Count} open order(s)");

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Preconditions: account is connected via ConnectByServerName/ConnectByHostPort.

var result = await _mt4.OpenedOrdersAsync(
    sortType: EnumOpenedOrderSortType.SortByOpenTimeAsc, // default
    deadline: null,
    cancellationToken: default);

foreach (var order in result.OrderInfos)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[{order.OrderType}] Ticket: {order.Ticket}, Symbol: {order.Symbol}, " +

                      $"OpenTime: {order.OpenTime}");
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
No required parameters.

Optional:

  • sortType (EnumOpenedOrderSortType) — sorting mode for returned orders. Default: SortByOpenTimeAsc. (Refer to your proto for the full enum list.)
  • deadline (DateTime?) — optional UTC deadline.
  • cancellationToken (CancellationToken) — optional cancellation token.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text:
Returns OpenedOrdersData with a collection of order information:

Field Type Description OrderInfos RepeatedField<OpenedOrderInfo> List of all currently opened orders.

Each OpenedOrderInfo includes (selected fields):

Field Type Description Ticket int Unique ticket ID for the order. Symbol string Trading symbol (e.g., "EURUSD"). Lots double Order volume in lots. OpenPrice double Price at which the order was opened. StopLoss double Stop-loss price (0 if none). TakeProfit double Take-profit price (0 if none). Profit double Current floating profit/loss. Swap double Accrued swap. Commision double Commission. MagicNumber int Expert/strategy magic number. OpenTime Timestamp Time the order was opened (server). OpenTimeUtc Timestamp Time the order was opened (UTC). OrderType OpenedOrderType Type of the order — see enum below.

docs.title: EnumOpenedOrderSortType — parameter sortType
docs.text:
• SortByOpenTimeAsc = 0 — by open time, ascending (default)
  • SortByOpenTimeDesc = 1 — by open time, descending
  • SortByOrderTicketIdAsc = 2 — by ticket id, ascending
  • SortByOrderTicketIdDesc = 3 — by ticket id, descending

docs.title: OpenedOrderType — field OrderType
docs.text:
• OoOpBuy = 0 — market buy
  • OoOpSell = 1 — market sell
  • OoOpBuylimit = 2 — pending buy limit
  • OoOpSelllimit = 3 — pending sell limit
  • OoOpBuystop = 4 — pending buy stop
  • OoOpSellstop = 5 — pending sell stop
  • OoOpBalance = 6 — balance operation (deposit/withdrawal)
  • OoOpCredit = 7 — credit operation

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method to retrieve and display the list of all currently open orders. Helpful for:

  • Monitoring active positions
  • Building dashboards with live order info
  • Analyzing exposure, floating P/L, and symbol distribution

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• IDs are int. If you hold tickets as long, validate the value fits into Int32 before calling close/modify APIs.
  • UTC times. OpenTime is UTC; convert only for UI.
  • Freshness before actions. Re-query right before sending Close/Modify/CloseBy to reduce race-condition errors.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Race conditions. Orders can be closed by other processes between list and action; handle ApiExceptionMT4 on follow-up calls.
  • Empty list ≠ error. No open orders returns an empty OrderInfos list.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path: Open a small order and verify it appears with expected Symbol, Lots, and non-zero Ticket.
  • Sorting check: Call with a different sortType (if available in your proto) and confirm order is reordered.
  • Failure path: Immediately close an order after listing and try to act on its ticket — expect a handled error on the next call.

docs.title: Sending a Market or Pending Order
docs.text:
Request: send a trade order (market or pending) Sends a new order using the specified parameters and returns execution details.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT4Account.OrderSendAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderSend (in the TradingHelper service)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) → OrderSendReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): TradingHelper.TradingHelperClient.OrderSend(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace mt4_term_api
{
    public class MT4Account
    {
        public async Task<OrderSendData> OrderSendAsync(
            OrderSendRequest request,
            DateTime? deadline = null,
            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    }
}

Request message:

OrderSendRequest { Symbol, OperationType, Volume, Price, Slippage, Stoploss, Takeprofit, MagicNumber, Comment }

Reply message:

OrderSendReply { data: OrderSendData }

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (typed, data-returning) ---
// Same OrderSendRequest shape as low-level; the service forwards and returns OrderSendData:
//   var sent = await _service.OrderSendAsync(request);   // request built below

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Preconditions: account is connected via ConnectByServerName/ConnectByHostPort.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));

var request = new OrderSendRequest
{
    Symbol       = "EURUSD",
    OperationType= OrderSendOperationType.OcOpBuy, // market BUY
    Volume       = 0.10,
    Price        = 0,   // market order -> 0 (server will use current price)
    Slippage     = 5,   // in points
    MagicNumber  = 123456,
    Comment      = "Test order"
};

var result = await _mt4.OrderSendAsync(
    request: request,
    deadline: null,
    cancellationToken: cts.Token);

Console.WriteLine($"The order was successfully opened. Ticket: {result.Ticket}, Price: {result.Price}");
// If your proto returns open time:
// Console.WriteLine($"OpenTime (UTC): {result.OpenTime}");

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
OrderSendRequest — fields:

Field Type Required Description Symbol string ✔️ Trading symbol (e.g., "EURUSD"). OperationType OrderSendOperationType ✔️ Order operation (market/pending). Volume double ✔️ Order volume in lots (> 0). Price double ➖ For pending orders — target price. For market — 0. Slippage int ➖ Max slippage allowed (in points). MagicNumber int ➖ Optional tag used to identify EA/strategy. Comment string ➖ Optional order comment (broker formats may vary).

docs.title: ENUM: OrderSendOperationType — field OperationType
docs.text:
Value Description OcOpBuy = 0 Market Buy OcOpSell = 1 Market Sell OcOpBuylimit = 2 Pending Buy Limit OcOpSelllimit = 3 Pending Sell Limit OcOpBuystop = 4 Pending Buy Stop OcOpSellstop = 5 Pending Sell Stop

Note the casing: pending members are OcOpBuylimit / OcOpSelllimit / OcOpBuystop / OcOpSellstop (lowercase after Op).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text:
OrderSendData — typical fields:

Field Type Description Ticket int Unique order ID assigned by MT4. Volume double Filled volume (lots). Price double Actual execution price (or pending price). OpenTime Timestamp Time when the order was opened.

The exact set of returned fields depends on your proto. The core fields are Ticket and Price (used in examples).

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: Place a new trade — market or pending — with control over volume, price, slippage, and attribution (magic/comment). The response includes the assigned ticket and execution price for confirmation and subsequent management.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Slippage units = points. Not pips. For 5‑digit FX, 1 pip = 10 points.
  • Validate volume & price. Use SymbolParams to read VolumeMin/Max/Step and Digits before sending.
  • Market vs Pending. For market orders set Price = 0; for pending you must set a valid Price relative to the current market.
  • MagicNumber hygiene. Use a stable magic per strategy to simplify ticket attribution and reconciliation.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Trade mode disabled. If TradeMode for the symbol forbids new orders, server will reject.
  • Wrong side/price for pending. e.g., BuyLimit above market or BuyStop below market → error.
  • Volume step. Non‑aligned Volume (not a multiple of VolumeStep) is rejected by many brokers.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path: Send a tiny market order on a demo (e.g., 0.01 lot); expect non‑zero Ticket and a reasonable Price.
  • Pending order: Place a BuyLimit well below current Bid; verify order appears in open/pending list with the requested price.
  • Failure path: Try Volume = 0 or invalid pending price and confirm you receive an ApiExceptionMT4 with a clear code without crashing the app.

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (typed, data-returning) ---
var hist = await _service.OrdersHistoryAsync(
    DateTime.UtcNow.AddDays(-7), DateTime.UtcNow);
Console.WriteLine($"{hist.OrdersInfo.Count} closed order(s)");

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Preconditions: account is connected via ConnectByServerName/ConnectByHostPort.

var from = DateTime.UtcNow.AddDays(-7);
var to   = DateTime.UtcNow;

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));

{

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
• sortType (EnumOrderHistorySortType) — sorting mode:

  • HistorySortByOpenTimeAsc

  • HistorySortByOpenTimeDesc
  • HistorySortByCloseTimeAsc

  • HistorySortByCloseTimeDesc

  • from (DateTime?) — start time (UTC). Optional; if omitted, server default applies.

  • to (DateTime?) — end time (UTC). Optional.

Optional paging:

  • page (int?) — page number (>= 1).
  • itemsPerPage (int?) — items per page (>= 1).

Common optional:

  • deadline (DateTime?) — per‑call deadline.
  • cancellationToken (CancellationToken) — cancellation control.

The client validates from <= to (when both present) and non‑negative paging values.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text:
Returns OrdersHistoryData with:

Field Type Description OrdersInfo RepeatedField<HistoryOrderInfo> List of historical (closed) orders.

Each HistoryOrderInfo includes (selected fields):

Field Type Description Ticket int Unique ID of the order. Symbol string Trading symbol (e.g., EURUSD). Lots double Volume of the order in lots. OpenPrice double Entry price. ClosePrice double Exit price. Profit double Realized profit/loss. Swap double Accrued swap. Commision double Commission. StopLoss double Stop-loss price (0 if none). TakeProfit double Take-profit price (0 if none). MagicNumber int Magic number (if set). Comment string Attached order comment. OrderType OpenedOrderType Order type — see enum below. OpenTime Timestamp Time the order was opened. CloseTime Timestamp Time the order was closed.

docs.title: OpenedOrderType — field OrderType
docs.text:
• OoOpBuy = 0 · OoOpSell = 1 — market buy/sell
  • OoOpBuylimit = 2 · OoOpSelllimit = 3 — pending limit
  • OoOpBuystop = 4 · OoOpSellstop = 5 — pending stop
  • OoOpBalance = 6 · OoOpCredit = 7 — balance/credit operations

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Retrieve completed trades within a given time window for:

  • Historical trade analysis
  • Auditing and reporting
  • Exporting logs for compliance/analytics

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• UTC throughout. Client sends timestamps as UTC; convert only at presentation.
  • Paginate large ranges. For long histories, use page/itemsPerPage to reduce payload and latency.
  • Sorting first, then paging. The sort is applied before pagination by the server/proto contract.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Reversed range. If from > to, the client throws a helpful error before calling the server.
  • Partial data windows. Broker servers may limit history depth; request smaller chunks if very old data is needed.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path: Request the last 7 days and verify non‑empty results on an active demo.
  • Edge cases: Call with from == to or omit both to check server defaults.
  • Paging: Request itemsPerPage = 5 and iterate pages; ensure deterministic ordering with a fixed sortType.

docs.title: Orders — Overview
docs.text: This section groups together methods for managing orders: creating, closing (directly or by opposite), and retrieving their details (live and historical). Use it for the full trade lifecycle.

docs.title: 📂 Methods in this folder
docs.text:
• OpenedOrders.md Get full details of all currently opened orders (ticket, symbol, lots, P/L, etc.).

  • OpenedOrderTickets.md Lightweight list of ticket IDs for opened orders.

  • OrdersHistory.md Retrieve closed trades within a specified time range (supports sorting).

  • OrderSend.md Example of sending a market/pending order with volume, slippage, comment, magic.

  • ModifyOrder.md Change an existing order's SL/TP, price or expiration by ticket.

  • CloseOrder.md Close (or delete) an order by its ticket and print server result/comment.

  • CloseByOrder.md Close one order by another opposite-direction order (hedged close-by).

docs.title: ⚡ Example Workflow (service wrapper)
docs.text:
// 1) Place an order (market or pending) -> returns OrderSendData with the ticket
var sent = await _service.OrderSendAsync(new OrderSendRequest {
    Symbol = "EURUSD", OperationType = OrderSendOperationType.OcOpBuy, Volume = 0.10, Slippage = 5 });

// 2) Monitor active positions
var opened  = await _service.OpenedOrdersAsync();
var tickets = await _service.OpenedOrdersTicketsAsync();

// 3) Option A: Close directly by ticket (sugar shortcut)
await _service.CloseByTicketAsync(sent.Ticket);
//    ...or raw: await _service.OrderCloseDeleteAsync(new OrderCloseDeleteRequest { OrderTicket = sent.Ticket });

// 4) Option B: Close by opposite order (hedged accounts only)
await _service.OrderCloseByAsync(new OrderCloseByRequest {
    TicketToClose = 123456, OppositeTicketClosingBy = 654321 });

// 5) Review historical performance for the past week
var history = await _service.OrdersHistoryAsync(DateTime.UtcNow.AddDays(-7), DateTime.UtcNow);

docs.title: ✅ Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Fetch before you act. Call OpenedOrders (or OpenedOrdersAsync) before attempting modify/close to ensure the ticket is valid and still open.
  2. CloseBy preconditions. Both tickets must be open, have equal volume, and be in opposite directions. Some brokers/accounts may disallow CloseBy.
  3. Deadlines & cancellation. Pass deadline/CancellationToken on long operations; the library applies sensible defaults but you can tighten or relax them.
  4. Error handling. Catch ApiExceptionMT4 and log broker/terminal error codes (e.g., invalid ticket, trade disabled, market closed, stops too close).
  5. Paging history. If you pull long ranges from OrdersHistoryAsync, use paging (page/itemsPerPage) to avoid huge payloads.
  6. Respect symbol rules. Use Market‑Info docs (Digits, VolumeMin/Max/Step, TradeMode) to validate orders before send/close.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Provide a compact toolkit for the order lifecycle:

  • Open → Monitor → Close/Delete → Audit.
  • Simplify UI/CLI workflows and automation.
  • Offer predictable timeouts, retries, and clear error surfaces.

👉 Use this overview as a map and follow links to each .md file for complete method details, parameters, enums, and pitfalls.

docs.title: Streaming Real-Time Quotes for a Symbol
docs.text:
Request: subscribe to real‑time bid/ask price updates for a given symbol Opens a streaming channel to receive tick‑by‑tick quotes as the market changes.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT4Account.OnSymbolTickAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnSymbolTick (in the SubscriptionService service)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) → stream OnSymbolTickReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): SubscriptionService.SubscriptionServiceClient.OnSymbolTick(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace mt4_term_api
{
    public class MT4Account
    {
        public async IAsyncEnumerable<OnSymbolTickData> OnSymbolTickAsync(
            IEnumerable<string> symbols,
            [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    }
}

Request message:

OnSymbolTickRequest { symbols: string[] }

Reply message:

OnSymbolTickReply { data: OnSymbolTickData } (server stream)

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (streaming; same shape as the low-level call below) ---
// The service forwards to the account:
//   await foreach (var t in _service.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[]{"EURUSD"}, ct)) { ... }

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Preconditions: account is connected via ConnectByServerName/ConnectByHostPort.
// Tip: always pass a CancellationToken; streams are infinite by design.
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
await foreach (var tick in _mt4.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
{
    var q = tick.SymbolTick;
    if (q == null) continue;

    Console.WriteLine($"Tick: {q.Symbol} {q.Bid}/{q.Ask} @ {q.Time}");
    break; // demo: leave after the first tick
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
OnSymbolTickAsync (service and low-level share the same signature)

Parameter Type Required Description symbols string[] ✅ One or more symbols (even a single one like new[]{"EURUSD"}). cancellationToken CancellationToken ❌ Cancels the infinite stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: Both variants deliver items of type SymbolTickData, which contains a QuoteData payload:

docs.title: Structure: QuoteData
docs.text:
Field Type Description Symbol string Symbol name Bid double Current bid price Ask double Current ask price Time string UTC timestamp of the tick

In the wrapper, the first received tick is printed to console and the method exits.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this to receive live market data for a symbol. Typical scenarios:

  • Real‑time quote panels
  • Alert engines that trigger on price movement
  • Feeding pricing into automated strategies/UI overlays

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Streams are infinite. Always pass a CancellationToken (wrapper adds a timeout guard).
  • Server Cancelled != app cancellation. Some servers respond with StatusCode.Cancelled when finalizing a subscription; client code treats this as graceful completion unless your token was cancelled with an error.
  • Reconnects. Transient transport issues (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal) are retried by the client’s internal stream wrapper with exponential backoff.
  • Many symbols? Prefer a single subscription with multiple symbols over many per‑symbol subscriptions.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• No first tick. If the market is closed/illiquid or symbol is wrong, you may hit the timeout without any tick. Validate symbol names exactly as returned by SymbolsAsync().
  • Over‑subscribing. Creating lots of simultaneous per‑symbol streams can exhaust chart/session limits on the terminal. Batch symbols where possible.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text:
• Happy path: You should see at least one tick during active market hours.
  • Timeout path: Use a tiny timeoutSeconds to verify graceful stop without exceptions.
  • Cancel path: Cancel the token and ensure the app exits the loop cleanly without leaking tasks.

docs.title: Streaming Terminal Connection State
docs.text:
Request: subscribe to terminal connection-state events via OnConnectState. Emits a snapshot whenever the terminal's connectivity/liveness changes — a heartbeat for your UI.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT4Account.OnConnectStateAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.Connection
  • Proto definition: OnConnectState (in the Connection service)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.Connection
  • Method: OnConnectState(OnConnectStateRequest) → stream OnConnectStateReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): Connection.ConnectionClient.OnConnectState(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace mt4_term_api
{
    public class MT4Account
    {
        public async IAsyncEnumerable<ConnectStateData> OnConnectStateAsync(
            [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct = default);
    }
}

Request message:

OnConnectStateRequest {}

Reply message:

OnConnectStateReply { data: ConnectStateData } (server stream)

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (streaming; same shape as low-level) ---
// await foreach (var s in _service.OnConnectStateAsync(ct)) { ... }

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Preconditions: account is connected via ConnectByServerName/ConnectByHostPort.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
await foreach (var state in _mt4.OnConnectStateAsync(cts.Token))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[{state.State}] connected={state.IsConnected} alive={state.IsAlive} api={state.ApiIsAlive} server={state.Server}");
    break; // demo: take the first snapshot
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
No required parameters.

Parameter Type Description ct CancellationToken Cancels the (open-ended) stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — ConnectStateData
docs.text: Field Type Description Id string Terminal instance id. State string Human-readable state (e.g. "Connected"). IsConnected bool Transport is connected. IsAlive bool Terminal process is alive. ApiIsAlive bool Terminal API is responsive. Server string Server name (e.g. "EGlobal-Demo"). Account ulong Account login. ErrorMessage string Error detail when state is not healthy (if any). Timestamp Timestamp Time of the snapshot.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Watch terminal connectivity in real time:

  • Drive a connection indicator in dashboards/CLIs.
  • Detect drops/reconnects and pause trading logic while not IsAlive/ApiIsAlive.
  • Log connectivity transitions for diagnostics.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Snapshot semantics. Each item is the current state; compute transitions on the client if you need edge events.
  • Healthy = all true. Treat IsConnected && IsAlive && ApiIsAlive as "ready to trade".
  • Endless stream. Always bound it with a CancellationToken; cancellation completes it gracefully.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Acting while not alive. Gate order placement on the healthy flags; sending during a drop yields transient errors.
  • Chatty logging. Don't log every identical snapshot — log on change.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. On a live connection the first snapshot has State="Connected" and all health flags true.
  • Transition. Briefly interrupt connectivity and verify the stream reports the unhealthy state, then recovery.

docs.title: Streaming Opened Order Profits
docs.text:
Request: subscribe to real-time stream of floating profit/loss per open order Starts a streaming channel to monitor floating profit for all active trades.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT4Account.OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnOpenedOrdersProfit (in the SubscriptionService service)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnOpenedOrdersProfit(OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest) → stream OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): SubscriptionService.SubscriptionServiceClient.OnOpenedOrdersProfit(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace mt4_term_api
{
    public class MT4Account
    {
        public async IAsyncEnumerable<OnOpenedOrdersProfitData> OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync(
            int intervalMs = 1000,
            [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct = default);
    }
}

Request message:

OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest { pullIntervalMilliseconds: int }

Reply message:

OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply { data: OnOpenedOrdersProfitData } (server stream)

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (streaming; same shape as low-level) ---
// await foreach (var upd in _service.OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync(1000, ct)) { ... }

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Preconditions: account is connected via ConnectByServerName/ConnectByHostPort.
// Tip: keep the interval modest to reduce load; cancel when you’re done.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
await foreach (var upd in _mt4.OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync(intervalMs: 1000, cts.Token))
{
    foreach (var o in upd.OpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdated)
        Console.WriteLine($"[P/L] #{o.Ticket} {o.Symbol} Lots={o.Lots} Profit={o.OrderProfit} Open={o.OpenPrice}");
    Console.WriteLine($"Equity={upd.AccountInfo?.Equity}");

    // For demo purposes we exit on first update;
    // in production remove this break to keep streaming.
    break;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
• intervalMs (int) — required. Polling interval in milliseconds between consecutive updates.
  • cancellationToken (CancellationToken, optional) — to cancel the streaming manually.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text:
Returns a stream (IAsyncEnumerable<OnOpenedOrdersProfitData>). Each item is a snapshot:

Field Type Description Type MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE Event group — see enum below. OpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdated RepeatedField<OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo> Per-order profit rows (below). AccountInfo OnEventAccountInfo Account snapshot (balance/equity/…). TerminalInstanceGuidId string Terminal instance id.

docs.title: OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo (each row)
docs.text: Field Type Description Ticket int Order ticket. Symbol string Symbol. Lots double Volume (lots). OpenPrice double Open price. OrderProfit double Current floating profit. Swap double Swap. Commission double Commission. OpenTime Timestamp Open time. MagicNumber int Magic number. Comment string Order comment.

docs.title: MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE — field Type
docs.text:
• OrderProfit = 0 — periodic profit update (this stream)
  • OrderUpdate = 1 — order create / modify / close

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
This method allows live monitoring of floating P/L per open order, enabling use cases such as:

  • Real-time UI dashboards showing per-trade profit
  • Risk monitoring systems
  • Alerting systems for high drawdown or profit conditions

It's optimized for continuous updates, with polling controlled by intervalMs.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Continuous stream: The method yields until you cancel via CancellationToken or exit your loop.
  • Reconnects on hiccups: Client logic restarts the stream on transient gRPC errors; brief gaps are normal during recovery.
  • Interval trade-off: Smaller intervalMs means more frequent updates and higher load; common values are 500–2000 ms.
  • Empty portfolio: With no open orders you may see few/no updates; this is expected—keep the stream or cancel.
  • Currency: Profit values are reported in the account currency.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Forgetting cancellation: Without a token or break condition, the loop runs indefinitely.
  • Too-aggressive intervals: Very small intervalMs can stress the terminal and your app.
  • Assuming tick timing: Updates follow your interval, not every market tick.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path: Open a small market order; verify that Profit fluctuates and ticket/symbol match.
  • Zero orders: Ensure your code handles the quiet stream without errors.
  • Cancellation: Cancel after a few seconds and confirm a clean shutdown (no unhandled exceptions).

docs.title: Streaming Opened Order Tickets
docs.text:
Request: subscribe to stream of currently open order ticket numbers Returns only the ticket IDs of all open orders as they change in real time.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT4Account.OnOpenedOrdersTicketsAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnOpenedOrdersTickets (in the SubscriptionService service)

  • Low‑level client (generated): SubscriptionService.SubscriptionServiceClient.OnOpenedOrdersTickets(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):

{
    public class MT4Account
    {
        public async IAsyncEnumerable<OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData> OnOpenedOrdersTicketsAsync(
            int intervalMs = 1000,
            [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct = default);

Request message:

OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest { pullIntervalMilliseconds: int }

OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply { data: OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData } (server stream)

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
// --- Service wrapper (streaming; same shape as low-level) ---
// await foreach (var upd in _service.OnOpenedOrdersTicketsAsync(1000, ct)) { ... }

// --- Low-level (direct account call) ---
// Periodic snapshots of the current ticket set; cancel when done.
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
await foreach (var update in _mt4.OnOpenedOrdersTicketsAsync(
    intervalMs: 1000,
    cancellationToken: cts.Token))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Positions: {string.Join(", ", update.PositionTickets)} | " +
                      $"Pending: {string.Join(", ", update.PendingOrderTickets)}");
    break; // demo: take first update only
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
• intervalMs (int) — required. Interval in milliseconds between each update.
  • cancellationToken (CancellationToken, optional) — token to cancel the stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text:
Returns a stream (IAsyncEnumerable<OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData>). Each item is a snapshot:

Field Type Description PositionTickets RepeatedField<int> Tickets of open market orders. PendingOrderTickets RepeatedField<int> Tickets of open pending orders. ServerTime Timestamp Server time of the snapshot. TerminalInstanceGuidId string Terminal instance id.

Each ticket corresponds to an active order in the terminal.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method to track open order IDs in real time, useful for:

  • Updating UI lists of active tickets
  • Detecting when new trades are opened or old ones closed
  • Triggering updates to related order details based on ticket change events

This is a lightweight alternative to streaming full order data, optimized for performance and minimal network load.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Snapshot-style updates. The stream returns the current ticket set at the chosen interval; compute diffs on the client if you need add/remove events.
  • Cancellation = clean finish. When you cancel the token, the stream completes gracefully (no exception needed in user code).
  • Reconnects on transport hiccups. Transient gRPC errors are retried internally with backoff up to a limit; short gaps are expected during restarts.
  • Pick a sensible interval. 500–2000 ms usually balances freshness and load for most UIs.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Races are normal. Orders can open/close between intervals; don’t assume you’ll see every intermediate state.
  • Large ticket sets. Many open orders can cause heavy UI updates each tick; debounce or diff before rendering.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path: With at least one open order, first snapshot contains that ticket.
  • Change detection: Open/close an order while streaming and verify your diffing logic spots adds/removes.
  • Timeout path: Use a short cancellation timeout to ensure your loop exits cleanly without unhandled exceptions.

  • cancellationToken (CancellationToken, optional) — used to cancel the stream manually.

Returns a stream (IAsyncEnumerable<OnTradeData>) where each item represents a trade event:

Field Type Description Type MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE Event group — see enum below. EventData OnTadeEventData The trade event payload (orders affected). AccountInfo OnEventAccountInfo Account snapshot at the event (equity, etc.). TerminalInstanceGuidId string Terminal instance that produced the event.

  • OrderUpdate = 1 — an order was created / modified / closed

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Subscribe to real-time trade activity — executed orders, closes, and other trade events sent by the server. Suitable for:

  • Live dashboards / client UIs
  • Post-trade hooks (logging, risk checks)
  • Auditing trade flow in automated systems

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• The stream is continuous — manage lifecycle with cancellation tokens.
  • Client performs auto-reconnect on transient gRPC errors; if you reprocess events after reconnect, deduplicate by Ticket + timestamps.

docs.title: Streaming — Overview
docs.text: This section groups real‑time streams from MT4: price ticks, trade events, and live snapshots of open orders (P/L or ticket lists). Use these when you need continuously updating data rather than one‑off RPC calls.

docs.title: 📂 Methods in this folder
docs.text:
• RealTimeQuotes.md Subscribe to tick‑by‑tick quotes for one or more symbols.

  • StreamOpenedOrderProfits.md Live stream of floating P/L for each open order (polling interval controlled by you).

  • StreamOpenedOrderTickets.md Lightweight stream that returns only the ticket IDs of currently open orders.

  • StreamTradeUpdates.md Server‑side stream of trade activity (executions/closures/etc.).

  • StreamConnectState.md Terminal connection-state heartbeat (connected/alive/api-alive).

docs.title: 1) Show the first live tick for a symbol
docs.text:
// Service (same shape as low-level):
//   await foreach (var tick in _service.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[]{"EURUSD"}, ct)) { ...; break; }

// Low-level: break on first item or cancel via token
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
await foreach (var tick in _mt4.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
{
    var q = tick.SymbolTick;
    Console.WriteLine($"Tick: {q.Symbol} {q.Bid}/{q.Ask} @ {q.Time}");
    break; // stop after first
}

docs.title: 2) Monitor floating P/L per open order
docs.text:
// Low-level: 1s interval, cancel on condition
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
_ = Task.Run(async () => { await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)); cts.Cancel(); });

await foreach (var upd in _mt4.OnOpenedOrdersProfitAsync(1000, cts.Token))
{
    foreach (var o in upd.OpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdated)
        Console.WriteLine($"{o.Symbol} #{o.Ticket} P/L={o.OrderProfit}");
}

docs.title: 3) Track when tickets change
docs.text:
await foreach (var update in _mt4.OnOpenedOrdersTicketsAsync(1000, ct))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Positions: {string.Join(", ", update.PositionTickets)} | Pending: {string.Join(", ", update.PendingOrderTickets)}");
}

docs.title: 4) Snapshot + streaming combo
docs.text:
// Get a snapshot first...
var syms = new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD" };
var snap = await _mt4.QuoteManyAsync(syms);
// ...then stream ticks to keep UI “live”
await foreach (var t in _mt4.OnSymbolTickAsync(syms, ct))
{
    // update widgets/pricing panels incrementally
}

docs.title: ✅ Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always pass a CancellationToken. Streams are open‑ended; you control their lifetime.
  2. Expect Cancelled on shutdown. Both client‑initiated and server‑initiated cancellations are normal termination paths.
  3. Choose sensible intervals. For OpenedOrderProfits/OpenedOrderTickets, 500–2000 ms is typical. Faster polling increases load.
  4. Backoff & reconnect. The client retries on transient gRPC statuses (Unavailable/DeadlineExceeded/Internal) with exponential backoff; persistent failures bubble up to you.

  5. Validate inputs.

  6. OnSymbolTickAsync requires at least one existing symbol (e.g., "EURUSD").

  7. Use the same casing and broker suffixes (EURUSD.m, XAUUSD-RAW) the server exposes.
  8. Keep prices raw for math; round only for display. Timestamps are UTC.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Streaming APIs power real‑time UIs, alerting, and automation:

  • Quotes: live panels, best‑bid/ask triggers, latency‑sensitive logic.
  • Opened orders: on‑the‑fly risk views (P/L), change detection via ticket lists.
  • Trades: immediate reaction to fills/closures for logging, analytics, or hedging.

Use this page as a map and dive into each file for signatures, fields, and examples.

docs.title: Strategies — Overview
docs.text: Ready-made orchestrators (single strategies) and a preset (an adaptive wrapper that picks one), all built on top of MT4Service and MT4Sugar. Use them as runnable examples and as a starting point for your own logic.

docs.title: 🛡️ Described by default — how to go live
docs.text:
Every orchestrator and the preset ship guarded. With Live = false (the default) they read the market, compute the plan and print it — no orders are sent. This is safe to run anywhere.

To actually trade, flip the flag:

  • In the menu — set Live = true on the entry in Program.cs (lines ~107–111), e.g. new GridOrchestrator(svc) { Symbol = sym, Live = true }.
  • Programmatically — set the property when you construct it: new ScalpOrchestrator(svc) { Live = true, RiskMoney = 20 }.

⚠️ Live places real orders on the configured account. Test on a demo you control — not on a shared account.

Run any of them from the examples menu (dotnet run) or directly: dotnet run -- --example=<N>.

docs.title: 🤖 Orchestrators (menu 6–9)
docs.text:
# Orchestrator Idea Instruments it uses 6 Scalp Risk-sized market entry + fixed TP, force-close after a hold market order, BuyMarketByRisk 7 Trailing Stop Risk-sized entry, ratchet the stop behind price market order + ModifySlTp 8 Grid Symmetric pending-limit grid around price pending limits (OcOpBuylimit/OcOpSelllimit) 9 Breakout Buy-stop + sell-stop straddle, keep the side that fills pending stops (OcOpBuystop/OcOpSellstop)

Each is a small, parametrized class: construct it, set properties, await ExecuteAsync(ct).

docs.title: 🧩 Presets (menu 10)
docs.text:
# Preset Idea 10 Adaptive Mode Reads the market (spread as a volatility proxy) + a floating-loss safety cap, then dispatches to Scalp (calm) or Trailing (volatile) with tuned parameters.

A preset is the next layer up: it chooses an orchestrator and its parameters for the current conditions.

docs.title: 🧱 Where they sit
docs.text:
MT4Service / MT4Sugar   ← the API the strategies call
      ↓
Orchestrators           ← one strategy each (Scalp, Trailing, Grid, Breakout)
      ↓
Presets                 ← pick + configure an orchestrator per market state

MT4 note: these are intentionally bounded to what MT4 offers (orders, pending orders, no DOM). They favor readable, guarded flows over completeness — copy one and adapt it.

docs.title: Breakout Orchestrator
docs.text:
A breakout straddle: a buy-stop above Ask and a sell-stop below Bid, each with SL/TP. Whichever side the market breaks fills; the orchestrator cancels the opposite pending and lets the position run. Flattens on timeout if nothing breaks.

  • Class: BreakoutOrchestrator (examples/Orchestrators/9_BreakoutOrchestrator.cs)
  • Menu: 9. ORCHESTRATOR: breakout — dotnet run -- --example=9
  • Builds on: MT4Service (OrderSendAsync with pending stops, OpenedOrdersAsync) + MT4Sugar (PriceFromOffsetPoints, NormalizePrice, CancelAllPending)

🛡️ Described by default (Live = false): prints the plan, sends nothing. Set Live = true to trade — see Strategies overview. Live places real orders.

docs.title: ⚙️ Parameters
docs.text: Property Default Meaning Symbol EURUSD Trading symbol. DistancePoints 200 How far above/below the market to place each stop. StopLossPoints 200 SL distance from the entry. TakeProfitPoints 400 TP distance from the entry. Volume 0.01 Volume per side (auto-normalized). MaxWaitSeconds 60 Wait this long for a breakout before flattening. PollSeconds 3 Seconds between trigger checks. Magic 4002 Magic-number tag. Live false When true, actually trades.

docs.title: 🔄 Flow
docs.text:
1. Compute BUY_STOP at DistancePoints above Ask and SELL_STOP the same below Bid, each with SL/TP.
  2. Live: send both as OrderSendAsync (OcOpBuystop / OcOpSellstop).
  3. Poll OpenedOrdersAsync every PollSeconds. When a market order (OoOpBuy/OoOpSell) appears, one side filled → CancelAllPendingAsync drops the opposite stop; the position runs to its SL/TP.
  4. If nothing breaks within MaxWaitSeconds → cancel both pendings.

docs.title: ▶️ Example (described)
docs.text:
+== BREAKOUT ORCHESTRATOR =====================================+
  EURUSD bid=1,11738 ask=1,118  BUY_STOP @ 1,12 / SELL_STOP @ 1,11539  vol=0,01  SL=200pt TP=400pt
  [described] would: place both stops (OcOpBuystop / OcOpSellstop) with SL/TP,
  then poll for a fill, cancel the opposite pending, and flatten on timeout. Set Live=true to run.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes
docs.text:
• One side wins. As soon as a stop fills (becomes a market order), the opposite pending is cancelled so you're not left with both sides.
  • SL/TP are on the pending. They travel with the order into the position — no second call needed after the fill.
  • Distance vs min stop. DistancePoints must exceed the broker's minimum stop distance from market.

docs.title: Grid Orchestrator
docs.text:
A symmetric pending-order grid around the current price — buy-limits below Ask and sell-limits above Bid, several levels each at a fixed spacing. A range / mean-reversion scaffold.

  • Class: GridOrchestrator (examples/Orchestrators/8_GridOrchestrator.cs)
  • Menu: 8. ORCHESTRATOR: grid — dotnet run -- --example=8
  • Builds on: MT4Service (OrderSendAsync with pending types) + MT4Sugar (PriceFromOffsetPoints, NormalizeVolume, CancelAllPending)

🛡️ Described by default (Live = false): prints the grid, sends nothing. Set Live = true to place it — see Strategies overview. Live places real pending orders.

docs.title: ⚙️ Parameters
docs.text: Property Default Meaning Symbol EURUSD Trading symbol. LevelsPerSide 3 Number of pending levels on each side. SpacingPoints 150 Spacing between levels, in points. Volume 0.01 Volume per pending order (auto-normalized). Magic 4001 Magic-number tag for the grid. Live false When true, actually places orders.

docs.title: 🔄 Flow
docs.text:
1. Snapshot the symbol; normalize the volume.
  2. For each level i = 1..LevelsPerSide: compute BUY_LIMIT at i × SpacingPoints below Ask and SELL_LIMIT the same above Bid (PriceFromOffsetPoints).
  3. Live: send each as OrderSendAsync with OcOpBuylimit / OcOpSelllimit.
  4. Demo cleanup: CancelAllPendingAsync(Symbol) clears the grid it just set.

docs.title: ▶️ Example (described)
docs.text:
+== GRID ORCHESTRATOR =========================================+
  EURUSD bid=1,11736 ask=1,11776  3 level(s)/side @ 150pt, vol=0,01
  [described] L1: BUY_LIMIT @ 1,11626   SELL_LIMIT @ 1,11886
  [described] L2: BUY_LIMIT @ 1,11476   SELL_LIMIT @ 1,12036
  [described] L3: BUY_LIMIT @ 1,11326   SELL_LIMIT @ 1,12186
  Set Live=true to place the grid (OcOpBuylimit / OcOpSelllimit), then CancelAllPendingAsync to clear.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes
docs.text:
• Uses pending orders directly. Sugar has no pending helper, so the grid builds OrderSendRequest with pending OperationType — see Enums.
  • Self-cleaning demo. The example cancels its own pendings after placing them; a real grid would leave them working and manage fills.
  • Spacing vs min stop. Keep SpacingPoints beyond the broker's minimum distance from market, or limits closest to price may be rejected.

docs.title: Scalp Orchestrator
docs.text:
Risk-sized market entry with a protective stop and a fixed take-profit, held for a short window, then force-closed. A quick in-and-out scaffold.

  • Class: ScalpOrchestrator (examples/Orchestrators/6_ScalpOrchestrator.cs)
  • Menu: 6. ORCHESTRATOR: scalp — dotnet run -- --example=6
  • Builds on: MT4Sugar (BuyMarketByRiskAsync, ModifySlTpAsync, CloseAllMarketAsync)

🛡️ Described by default (Live = false): prints the plan, sends nothing. Set Live = true to trade — see Strategies overview. Live places real orders.

docs.title: ⚙️ Parameters
docs.text: Property Default Meaning Symbol EURUSD Trading symbol. IsBuy true Direction (true = BUY, false = SELL). RiskMoney 20 Money risked over the stop distance (deposit currency). StopPoints 150 Stop distance in points (also drives risk sizing). TakeProfitPoints 300 Take-profit distance in points. MaxHoldSeconds 30 Force-close after this long if SL/TP hasn't triggered. Live false When true, actually trades.

docs.title: 🔄 Flow
docs.text:
1. Snapshot the symbol; size the volume from RiskMoney over StopPoints (CalcVolumeForRisk).
  2. Live: BuyMarketByRiskAsync / SellMarketByRiskAsync — opens with a protective SL StopPoints away.
  3. Attach the take-profit (ModifySlTp).
  4. Hold up to MaxHoldSeconds, checking whether it closed on its own (SL/TP hit).
  5. Flatten any remainder (CloseAllMarket).

docs.title: ▶️ Example (described)
docs.text:
+== SCALP ORCHESTRATOR =========================================+
  EURUSD BUY  risk=$20 over 150pt -> 0,13 lot(s)
  SL=150pt  TP=300pt  maxHold=30s  spread=1,0pt
  [described] would: open-by-risk -> attach TP -> hold -> force-close. Set Live=true to run.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes
docs.text:
• Risk-first sizing. Volume comes from your money risk and the stop distance, not a fixed lot.
  • Tune for volatility. Tight stops/short holds for calm markets; widen both when it's choppy.
  • Guarded. Keep Live = false while you tune parameters.

docs.title: Trailing-Stop Orchestrator
docs.text:
Risk-sized market entry protected by a trailing stop: once price has moved far enough in favor, the stop ratchets to lock in gains, staying a fixed distance behind price. Exits on stop-out or timeout.

  • Class: TrailingStopOrchestrator (examples/Orchestrators/7_TrailingStopOrchestrator.cs)
  • Menu: 7. ORCHESTRATOR: trailing stop — dotnet run -- --example=7
  • Builds on: MT4Sugar (BuyMarketByRiskAsync, ModifySlTpAsync) + MT4Service (QuoteAsync, OpenedOrdersTicketsAsync)

🛡️ Described by default (Live = false): prints the plan, sends nothing. Set Live = true to trade — see Strategies overview. Live places real orders.

docs.title: ⚙️ Parameters
docs.text: Property Default Meaning Symbol EURUSD Trading symbol. IsBuy true Direction (BUY trails the stop up, SELL trails it down). RiskMoney 20 Money risked over the initial stop. StopPoints 200 Initial stop distance in points (and risk-sizing basis). TrailStartPoints 150 Profit (points) required before the stop starts trailing. TrailDistancePoints 100 Distance the trailing stop keeps behind price. MaxHoldSeconds 60 Force-close after this long. PollSeconds 3 Seconds between trailing checks. Live false When true, actually trades.

docs.title: 🔄 Flow
docs.text:
1. Risk-size and open a market order with an initial SL (BuyMarketByRiskAsync / SellMarketByRiskAsync).
  2. Poll the quote every PollSeconds. Once profit ≥ TrailStartPoints, move the SL to TrailDistancePoints behind price only if it improves (ModifySlTp).
  3. If the market takes out the trailing stop (ticket gone) → done.
  4. On MaxHoldSeconds timeout → flatten (CloseAllMarket).

docs.title: ▶️ Example (described)
docs.text:
+== TRAILING-STOP ORCHESTRATOR =================================+
  EURUSD BUY  risk=$20 over 200pt -> 0,1 lot(s)
  trail: start after 150pt, keep 100pt behind; maxHold=60s
  [described] would: open-by-risk -> poll quote -> ratchet SL via ModifySlTp -> exit. Set Live=true to run.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes
docs.text:
• Only tightens. The stop never loosens — it moves to lock profit, never widens risk.
  • TrailStartPoints ≥ broker min stop. Don't start trailing closer than the broker's minimum stop distance.
  • Poll cadence. Faster PollSeconds reacts sooner but adds load; 2–5 s is typical.

docs.title: Adaptive Mode Preset
docs.text:
A preset is the layer above orchestrators: it reads the market and picks one. Adaptive Mode checks a floating-loss safety cap, then uses spread as a volatility proxy to dispatch to Scalp (calm) or Trailing (volatile) with tuned parameters.

  • Class: AdaptiveModePreset (examples/Presets/10_AdaptiveModePreset.cs)
  • Menu: 10. PRESET: adaptive mode — dotnet run -- --example=10
  • Builds on: the Scalp and Trailing orchestrators + MT4Sugar (GetTotalProfitLossAsync, GetSymbolSnapshotAsync)

🛡️ Described by default (Live = false): the chosen orchestrator only describes its plan. Live flows down to it — set Live = true to trade. See Strategies overview. Live places real orders.

docs.title: ⚙️ Parameters
docs.text: Property Default Meaning Symbol EURUSD Trading symbol. CalmSpreadPoints 20 Spread at/below which the market counts as calm → Scalp. RiskMoney 20 Base money risk per trade. MaxFloatingLoss -100 Abort before trading if current floating P/L is worse than this. Live false Flows down to the chosen orchestrator.

docs.title: 🔄 Flow
docs.text:
1. Safety cap. Read floating P/L (GetTotalProfitLossAsync). If it's below MaxFloatingLoss, stand down — don't add risk on a bleeding book.
  2. Analyze. Read the symbol snapshot; compare SpreadPoints to CalmSpreadPoints.
  3. Dispatch:
  4. Calm (spread ≤ cap) → ScalpOrchestrator (150pt stop, 300pt TP, 30s hold).
  5. Volatile (spread > cap) → TrailingStopOrchestrator with reduced risk (RiskMoney × 0.7), wider stop and a trailing exit.
  6. The chosen orchestrator runs (described or live per Live).

docs.title: ▶️ Example (described)
docs.text:
+== ADAPTIVE MODE PRESET =======================================+
  floating P/L = 10,58 (cap -100)
  EURUSD spread=1,0pt -> CALM
  mode: SCALP (tight spread)
+== SCALP ORCHESTRATOR =========================================+
  EURUSD BUY  risk=$20 over 150pt -> 0,13 lot(s)
  ...

docs.title: 🧩 Notes
docs.text:
• Spread is a cheap proxy. It's a stand-in for volatility; a production preset would use historical bar ranges.
  • Safety first. The floating-loss cap runs before any analysis — it can veto the whole cycle.
  • Compose your own. A preset is just "read state → choose orchestrator → set parameters". Copy this one and change the rules.

============================================================================ PublicAccount: publish the MT4 account in the "id" header as a public master account for copy trading on mrpc.pro, change its public name and profit share, unpublish it, and read its public status. The call needs only the "APIKey" header (your mrpc_live_ key) and the "id" header (the terminal), like every other terminal call: no user key, no session, no admin key. The account must belong to the API key's user and be an MT4 account (mt4.mrpc.pro); any other id - another user's account, a deleted one, an MT5 one, an unknown one - is answered PUBLIC_ACCOUNT_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND. The rules are the control panel's (mrpc.pro/my, "Public profile"): a public name of 2-32 letters, digits, spaces, "." "_" "-", and a profit share of 0-50 % (one decimal) charged to followers on winning copied trades. The terminal does not have to be running; the leaderboard lists the account once its first figures have been read from it (listed), which needs it connected. ============================================================================ class PublicAccountData class PublicAccountPublishRequest class PublicAccountReply class PublicAccountStatusRequest class PublicAccountUnpublishRequest class QuoteData static class QuoteHistory ============================================================================ Quote history: the bars a chart is drawn from, for one symbol - returned by PAGE, oldest first. MetaTrader 4 keeps no tick history, so there is no Ticks call here; the MT5 API has one. Bars walks a time range forward. A page carries at most page_size bars and, when the range holds more, a next_page_token; passing that token back (same symbol, timeframe and range) returns the next page. An empty next_page_token means the range is exhausted. Tokens are opaque: a client stores and returns them, nothing else. History lives in the terminal and is fetched from the broker on demand. The first request for a symbol or a period the terminal has not loaded yet can take a few seconds, and when the broker has not delivered it within that time the call answers with an error whose error_code is QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY - ask again a moment later. Every call needs the terminal id header ("id"), like every other call. ============================================================================ class QuoteHistoryBar One bar (candle), named as MQL4 names the fields of MqlRates. class QuoteHistoryBarsData class QuoteHistoryBarsReply class QuoteHistoryBarsRequest class QuoteHistoryData class QuoteHistoryReply class QuoteHistoryRequest class QuoteManyData class QuoteManyReply class QuoteManyRequest class QuoteReply class QuoteRequest enum QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME Timeframe of a bar. The value is the bar length in MINUTES - the same numbers MQL4's ENUM_TIMEFRAMES uses. These are the nine periods MT4 has. The names carry the prefix QHB_ (not QH_ as on MT5) because the older MarketInfo.QuoteHistory of MT4 already owns QH_PERIOD_M1..MN1 (ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME, other numbers) and enum value names are shared by the whole package. class ReconnectData class ReconnectReply class ReconnectRequest class RunningEaInfo class ScreenshotData class ScreenshotReply class ScreenshotRequest static class ServerTimezone ============================================================================ ServerTimezone: the broker server's time zone the platform uses for this account, and where it came from. docs.text: name description virtual ActiveTerminals(…) Active terminals running on THIS pod. virtual ActiveTerminalsCluster(…) Active terminals across ALL pods of this StatefulSet/Deployment. Lists peer pods via the Kubernetes API, then calls ActiveTerminals on each. virtual CaptureSessionScreenshot(…) Screenshot of a Windows interactive session's whole desktop - a specific MrpcTerminalUser<N> session, or (if session_user_name is empty) the pod's main/autologon session, the one startup.bat runs in. virtual CaptureSessionScreenshotOnPod(…) Same as CaptureSessionScreenshot, but fanned out from THIS pod to a DIFFERENT pod by IP (mirroring the ActiveTerminalsCluster fan-out) - a browser can only reach the pod that is currently serving it, not other pods' ClusterIPs, so the cluster admin view asks whichever pod it's connected to relay the request. virtual Drain(…) Puts THIS pod into the draining state ahead of shutdown (StatefulSet preStop hook). While draining the pod stops renewing its terminal ownership leases, suppresses crash persistence for terminals ending with the VM, and starts no new work; peers restore its terminals once the leases expire. One-way for the lifetime of the process; calling it again reports already_draining. virtual GetAllLogs(…) One-shot bundle of EVERY diagnostic log available on this pod: every *.log file on the shared Data folder AND in C:\OEM, plus the Windows Application + System event logs. docs.title: AdminApi class
docs.text:
============================================================ Admin / diagnostics service (terminal-agnostic — identical to the mt5 copy). Auth via admin_key (matched against the ADMIN_KEY env setting). HTTP-transcoded for the /admin HTML page + cross-pod fan-out, but HIDDEN from Swagger (excluded in SwaggerGen DocInclusionPredicate in Program.cs). NOTE: this file exists ONLY so the mt4 client libraries (create-grpc-libs, proto/mt4) include the admin API, matching mt5. The Terminal Manager binary compiles the single shared mrpc_admin proto from proto/mt5 (see the csproj) — do NOT add this file to the csproj or mrpc_admin.* would be defined twice. ============================================================

docs.title: AdminApi.AdminApiClient.Drain method (1 of 2)
docs.text:
Puts THIS pod into the draining state ahead of shutdown (StatefulSet preStop hook). While draining the pod stops renewing its terminal ownership leases, suppresses crash persistence for terminals ending with the VM, and starts no new work; peers restore its terminals once the leases expire. One-way for the lifetime of the process; calling it again reports already_draining.

public virtual DrainReply Drain(DrainRequest request, CallOptions options)
parameter description request The request to send to the server. options The options for the call.

docs.title: AdminApi.AdminApiClient.RefreshMrpcRest method (1 of 2)
docs.text:
Runs, in-process (LocalSystem, no guest logon/SSH needed), the same refresh startup.bat performs on a successful ONLOGON boot: robocopy published-app (including mrpc-rest) from the host share, then create/start MrpcRestService. Exists because ONLOGON is unreliable (autologon-dependent) - this lets a stuck deploy be repaired through the Terminal Manager's own already-running gRPC/HTTP API instead of waiting on that trigger or requiring interactive guest access.

public virtual RefreshMrpcRestReply RefreshMrpcRest(ActiveTerminalsRequest request, 
    CallOptions options)
parameter description request The request to send to the server. options The options for the call.

Stops THIS pod's local copy of one terminal (pod-to-pod: user-stop fan-out, duplicate prune, rebalance migration). Local only: never forwarded to another pod and never persisted to UserTerminals (the caller records any stop intent). cause is a StopCause name; only customer/API/admin/delete/test stops and InternalReap are accepted. Callers must check reply.error.

public virtual StopTerminalLocalReply StopTerminalLocal(StopTerminalLocalRequest request, 
    CallOptions options)
parameter description request The request to send to the server. options The options for the call.

AccountMarginLevel { get; set; } Margin level in percent, equity / margin * 100 (ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL); 0 when no margin is used. AccountMarginMode { get; set; } Always hedging on MT4 (several positions per symbol); present for parity with MT5. AccountTradeAllowed { get; set; } The account may trade (ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED); is_investor is its negation. Unset while the account is not connected yet and no offset is known. ServerTimeUtc { get; set; } server_time in UTC (the same moment; server_time is in the broker server's time zone). ServerUtcOffsetSeconds { get; set; } The broker server's offset from UTC in seconds, positive = ahead of UTC: validated by the terminal (a multiple of 15 minutes). Information, never converted; it is the offset behind every *_utc field of this API. ABSENT (has_server_utc_offset_seconds is false) while it is not known yet: the account is not connected, or it is connected but the market is closed and no price quote has arrived since the terminal started - MT4 learns the offset from a live quote. Absent never means UTC+0 (a UTC+0 broker sends 0 and has it present). The *_utc fields stay unset until it is known. A connected terminal whose computer clock is provably wrong answers SERVER_TIMEZONE_UNDETERMINED instead of data. The current offset is applied to every value, so history from before the broker's last daylight-saving change is off by the daylight-saving step (usually 3600 s). UtcServerTimeShiftMinutes { get; set; } The broker server's offset from UTC in whole minutes (server_utc_offset_seconds / 60), a multiple of 15. Information, never converted. 0 while the account is not connected yet. docs.title: Accounts class
docs.text:
============================================================================ Accounts: the MT4 accounts (terminals) that belong to your API key. This is the call to make when you need the terminal ids of accounts that already exist - started from the dashboard or by an earlier ConnectEx - so that you can send them as the "id" header of every other call. Unlike the terminal calls it needs NO "id" header: it is answered from the platform's records of the API key sent in the "APIKey" header, and it never starts, wakes or bills a terminal. Accounts are listed newest first (by started_utc, then terminal_id) and returned by page. Only accounts of THIS platform's endpoint are listed (mt5.mrpc.pro lists MT5 accounts, mt4.mrpc.pro lists MT4 accounts). ============================================================================

docs.title: PublicAccount class
docs.text:
============================================================================ PublicAccount: publish the MT4 account in the "id" header as a public master account for copy trading on mrpc.pro, change its public name and profit share, unpublish it, and read its public status. The call needs only the "APIKey" header (your mrpc_live_ key) and the "id" header (the terminal), like every other terminal call: no user key, no session, no admin key. The account must belong to the API key's user and be an MT4 account (mt4.mrpc.pro); any other id - another user's account, a deleted one, an MT5 one, an unknown one - is answered PUBLIC_ACCOUNT_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND. The rules are the control panel's (mrpc.pro/my, "Public profile"): a public name of 2-32 letters, digits, spaces, "." "_" "-", and a profit share of 0-50 % (one decimal) charged to followers on winning copied trades. The terminal does not have to be running; the leaderboard lists the account once its first figures have been read from it (listed), which needs it connected. ============================================================================

docs.title: QuoteHistory class
docs.text:
============================================================================ Quote history: the bars a chart is drawn from, for one symbol - returned by PAGE, oldest first. MetaTrader 4 keeps no tick history, so there is no Ticks call here; the MT5 API has one. Bars walks a time range forward. A page carries at most page_size bars and, when the range holds more, a next_page_token; passing that token back (same symbol, timeframe and range) returns the next page. An empty next_page_token means the range is exhausted. Tokens are opaque: a client stores and returns them, nothing else. History lives in the terminal and is fetched from the broker on demand. The first request for a symbol or a period the terminal has not loaded yet can take a few seconds, and when the broker has not delivered it within that time the call answers with an error whose error_code is QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY - ask again a moment later. Every call needs the terminal id header ("id"), like every other call. ============================================================================

docs.title: ServerTimezone class
docs.text:
============================================================================ ServerTimezone: the broker server's time zone the platform uses for this account, and where it came from. Every *_utc field of the API is the broker server time minus this offset. Answered by the platform itself from what it knows (the terminal is not asked unless nothing is known yet), so it is cheap to call. ============================================================================

TickValueWithSizeRequest(…) SymbolNames { get; } Symbols to read, by exact name (REST: repeated query parameter symbolNames). Each named symbol is added to Market Watch when it is not there yet, then read. At most 1000 names per request; a longer list is answered with an error. It is NOT "all symbols of the server": the terminal's Market Watch holds at most ~1000 symbols, so serving the server's list (12,000+ at some brokers) would mean adding all of them to Market Watch and changing the user's selection. Name the symbols you need. docs.title: AccountSummaryData.ServerUtcOffsetSeconds property
docs.text:
The broker server's offset from UTC in seconds, positive = ahead of UTC: validated by the terminal (a multiple of 15 minutes). Information, never converted; it is the offset behind every *_utc field of this API. ABSENT (has_server_utc_offset_seconds is false) while it is not known yet: the account is not connected, or it is connected but the market is closed and no price quote has arrived since the terminal started - MT4 learns the offset from a live quote. Absent never means UTC+0 (a UTC+0 broker sends 0 and has it present). The *_utc fields stay unset until it is known. A connected terminal whose computer clock is provably wrong answers SERVER_TIMEZONE_UNDETERMINED instead of data. The current offset is applied to every value, so history from before the broker's last daylight-saving change is off by the daylight-saving step (usually 3600 s).

public int ServerUtcOffsetSeconds { get; set; }

docs.title: TickValueWithSizeRequest.SymbolNames property
docs.text:
Symbols to read, by exact name (REST: repeated query parameter symbolNames). Each named symbol is added to Market Watch when it is not there yet, then read. At most 1000 names per request; a longer list is answered with an error. EMPTY list = every symbol currently in Market Watch. It is NOT "all symbols of the server": the terminal's Market Watch holds at most ~1000 symbols, so serving the server's list (12,000+ at some brokers) would mean adding all of them to Market Watch and changing the user's selection. Name the symbols you need.

public RepeatedField<string> SymbolNames { get; }
